383YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.d: Senators were chosen for Astolat, Bregasland, Hercynia, Kallavesa, Madruga, Miekarova, Mitwold, Necropolis, Ossium, Skarsind, Temeschwar and Therunin. The Senate appointed three ambassadors (to Axos, Jarm and the Iron Confederacy), ten generals and several other titles. The Synod returned cardinals, inquisitors and other religious positions, led by Leonora van Holberg as Patron of the Pavilion with 177 votes. Bourse auctions placed great forests and wayleaves, the largest bid being 510 thrones for the Golden Trees of Seren. Bourse votes filled further posts. The Conclave chose four grandmasters, and candidates declared for several titles, including the Archmages of Night and Winter and the Imperial Seer.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senate seat for Astolat went to Bohemond De Rondell, and Tancred was appointed General of the Hounds of Glory.
n.Highguard: Highguard returned Eli as Senator for Necropolis, and Asenath was appointed General of the Granite Pillar.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs chose Rurik as Senator for Skarsind, and Zerk was appointed General of the Summer Storm.
n.Navarr: Navarr filled two senate seats, Rhisiart Dancewalker for Hercynia and Travid Longest Path for Therunin, and Iron Osric was appointed General of the Green Shield.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast returned Chiara Zayden Riqueza as Senator for Madruga.
n.The League: The League chose Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar as Senator for Temeschwar, and Natalia "The Falcon" Barossa was appointed General of the Towerjacks.
n.The Marches: The Marches filled two senate seats, Orrick for Bregasland and William Lowther for Mitwold, and Jack Flint was appointed General of the Strong Reeds.
n.Varushka: Varushka returned Yulia Kasimirova Voronov for Miekarova and Vesna (Sparrow) Borkovna for Ossium. New generals were appointed for the Golden Axe, the Iron Helms and the Northern Eagle.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark chose Rane Sherarding as Senator for Kallavesa, and Rykana was appointed General of the Winter Sun.

t.Astolat: Bohemond De Rondell was elected Senator for Astolat.
t.Bregasland: Orrick was elected Senator for Bregasland.
t.Hercynia: Rhisiart Dancewalker was elected Senator for Hercynia.
t.Kallavesa: Rane Sherarding was elected Senator for Kallavesa.
t.Madruga: Chiara Zayden Riqueza was elected Senator for Madruga.
t.Miekarova: Yulia Kasimirova Voronov was elected Senator for Miekarova.
t.Mitwold: William Lowther was elected Senator for Mitwold.
t.Necropolis: Eli was elected Senator for Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Vesna (Sparrow) Borkovna was elected Senator for Ossium.
t.Skarsind: Rurik was elected Senator for Skarsind.
t.Temeschwar: Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar was elected Senator for Temeschwar.
t.Therunin: Travid Longest Path was elected Senator for Therunin.

383YE Winter Solstice Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 1994 thrones. The Senate funded Marcher military resupply and the enlargement of the Drakes, and set the magistrates on Brass Coast smuggling and on followers of Yaw'nagrah, which costs every mana site one crystal while the investigation runs. It renamed the Imperial Orc Wayleave as Legion Engineer and raised Holberg's upkeep to educate the Sand Fisher orcs. Commissions included works in Casinea, Hahnmark, Kallavesa, Kahraman, Sarvos, Tassato, Semmerholm and Hercynia, and a schloss ceded to the Commonwealth. Title-holders announced a spy network in Feroz, a ward against the trogoni and the decommissioning of Ossium's spy network. Three ambassadors were appointed and two deferred.

n.Dawn: Semmerholm gained the Arbor of the Twin Roses, a sinecure honouring the exemplar Elayne Silverlark whose Voice is chosen by the Dawnish National Assembly. The proposed Manor of the Greenwood failed.
n.Grendel: A spy network was announced for Grendel-held Feroz, and the Broken Shore Mithril Market in Cargo was commissioned to buy Grendel mithril in exchange for weirwood.
n.Highguard: The College of Maykop was commissioned in Casinea, and Britta's Shrine is to become a memorial for pilgrims of Courage, following a Highborn National Assembly judgement. A first version of that motion from Reikos was withdrawn.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Wayleave was renamed Legion Engineer and given power to build spy networks. Ka'bal used the title to announce a spy network in Feroz.
n.Navarr: The Tenebrous Path sinecure was commissioned in Hercynia to inspire the Thorns of Navarr, as the anti-vallorn army Isaella's Dance prepares to muster at Miaren. Navarr senators also launched the magistrates' hunt for followers of Yaw'nagrah.
n.The Brass Coast: The Parador of Dust in Kahraman was refurbished as a mithril ministry for the Freeborn. A schloss off Madruga was ceded to the Commonwealth, and magistrates were tasked with stopping smuggling across Brass Coast borders.
n.The League: League territories gained the Sweetwater Springs in Sarvos, an Imperial Consulate in Tassato and an expanded Georgie's House in Holberg. Holberg's upkeep also rose to educate the Sand Fisher orcs.
n.The Marches: The Senate disbursed 300 thrones to Orrick of Bregasland for military resupply and 230 thrones to complete the enlargement of the Drakes, the first Marcher army. Upwold's senator proposed the Thule treaty.
n.Thule: The ratified treaty ceded the regions of Miechernya in Miekarova and Webwood in Ossium to the Thule. Appointing an Ambassador to Otkodov was deferred to the Spring Equinox.
n.Urizen: The Senate commissioned an appraisal of fortifications in Urizen territory, to be delivered before Spring 384YE. Octavius of Damakan's Forge also announced the Broken Shore Mithril Market in Cargo, with its Broker chosen by Urizen mana site holders.
n.Varushka: Varushkan senators now appoint the five Ossium spoils-of-war positions, but Varushka lost Miechernya and Webwood to the Thule under the treaty. Ossium's spy network was decommissioned.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's runesmiths were confirmed as heirs of the Gildenheim Runeforge, and its ruins are to go to Runegrott. The Senate also commissioned the Kauppahall in Hahnmark and the Healing House of Wittal Grove in Kallavesa.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Urizen fortifications appraisal and seconded the Britta's Memorial motion.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Gildenheim Runeforge motion and seconded the Sweetwater Springs.
t.Bregasland: Orrick of Bregasland received 300 thrones for military resupply. The Quartermaster General's instruction to apply the Guerdon to Bregasland was ignored because it is not an army or military opportunity.
t.Casinea: A campus for the Halls of Maykop, the College of Maykop, was commissioned in Casinea.
t.Feroz: The Legion Engineer Ka'bal announced the construction of a spy network in Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: The Kauppahall trading hall was commissioned in Hahnmark, and the Runeforge excavation will cut the cost of a runeforge at Runegrott. The Runic Hearth of Adamant is meant to stop trogoni threatening Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: The Tenebrous Path sinecure, which produces mana crystals, was commissioned in Hercynia's Old Ranging. The Guerdon instruction naming Hercynia was ignored, and its senator's second seconding was referred to the magistrates.
t.Holberg: Holberg's upkeep rose by 14 thrones a season to educate the Sand Fisher orcs, and Georgie's House there was expanded. Two von Holberg citizens donated thrones to the treasury.
t.Kahraman: The Parador of Dust in the Jade Range was commissioned as a mithril ministry, with its Mistress appointed through the Bourse.
t.Kallavesa: The Healing House of Wittal Grove was commissioned in Kallavesa at 328 thrones, and its senator seconded the Runeforge excavation.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Ossium positions motion and seconded the Lyceum Schloss.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Champions of Virtue titles and seconded the Silver Chalice manifesto amendment.
t.Madruga: The Commonwealth may build a schloss for Lyceum visitors on the island east of Siroc, and the structure is ceded to them.
t.Miaren: Isaella's Dance is to muster at Miaren in the coming summer, and the Runic Hearth of Adamant is meant to protect Miaren from the trogoni. Its senator proposed the Yaw'nagrah investigation.
t.Miekarova: The Thule treaty ceded Miekarova's region of Miechernya to the Thule.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: its senator William Lowther proposed, and received, 230 thrones for materials to enlarge the Drakes.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the Urizen fortifications appraisal and proposed an Ambassador to the Thule.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the smuggling investigation, receiving 25 thrones for it, and proposed the Ambassador to Axos.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the withdrawn Britta's Shrine motion and proposed the Ambassador to Jarm.
t.Ossium: Ossium's spoils of war became Varushkan national positions and its Webwood region was ceded to the Thule. Its spy network was decommissioned and emergency repair of the Tower of the Scorpion was allowed.
t.Redoubt: The Architects of Stone at Delving in Redoubt prompted the appraisal of fortifications in Urizen territory, due before Spring 384YE.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the withdrawn Britta's Shrine motion and seconded the Arbor of the Twin Roses.
t.Sarvos: The Sweetwater Springs, a great work of wells and fountains to protect Sarvos against fire, was commissioned at 150 thrones.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy.
t.Semmerholm: The Arbor of the Twin Roses sinecure was commissioned in Semmerholm, but the Manor of the Greenwood and its Greenforest Market expansion failed.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the successful Britta's Memorial motion and seconded the Kauppahall.
t.Tassato: An Imperial Consulate was commissioned in Tassato with 250 thrones.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar is among the territories the Runic Hearth of Adamant is meant to shield from the trogoni. Its senator proposed the Cathedral of the Navigators.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the Yaw'nagrah investigation and proposed an Ambassador to the Commonwealth.
t.Upwold: Upwold's senator proposed the Thule treaty, and the Runic Hearth of Adamant is meant to protect Upwold from the trogoni.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the Ossium positions motion and proposed the College of Maykop.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Arbor of the Twin Roses and seconded the failed Manor of the Greenwood.

r.Holberg/Holfried: The Kennels of Holfried, Georgie's House, were expanded to sell across the Empire, raising the sinecure's revenue.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: The Healing House of Wittal Grove, a great work to benefit herb garden owners, was commissioned along with a title meant for a grimnir. A motion allowing the Senate to abrogate that title failed.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Miechernya was ceded to the Thule under the ratified treaty.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Webwood was ceded to the Thule under the ratified treaty.

383YE Winter Solstice Synod judgements.d: Rafael Barossa di Tassato's mandate chastising the Wisdom assembly passed, but rival mandates from the Wisdom, Loyalty and Courage assemblies left the matter of mandate opposition unresolved. Several weaker mandates were enacted only because of the ongoing pilgrimage in Imperatrix Lisabetta's name. Other mandates backed the Brass Coast's abandonment of Feroz, Sarvos becoming the City of Masks, wardens and wagon-raiders in Ossium, a Marcher raid on Skallahn, and cooperation with the Grendel in Spiral. Many Whittlefolk were condemned for blasphemy. Yulia was revoked as senator for Miekarova. Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra was vindicated and became High Exorcist, and the virtue fund closed at 60 Thrones.

n.Dawn: Dawnish mandates challenged other nations to a race for the Barrens, rewarded knights fighting to reclaim Dark Ranging, sent knights-errant to join the Varushkan wagon raiders in Ossium, and invited Marracossan refugees to the House of the Proffered Hand in Astolat.
n.Druj: The Druj were the target of crusade calls from League and General Assembly priests, of a contest between Dawn, Highguard and the Imperial Orcs to seize the Barrens, and of mandates to hunt their guerrillas and their Webwood temple in Ossium.
n.Grendel: Urizen urged its citizens to extend the mithril block's protection to Grendel settlements without revealing its workings, and a mandate strengthened by Loyalty told the Urizeni of Spiral to cooperate and trade with the Salt Lord. The Freeborn were urged to abandon Feroz, which had been surrendered to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highguard's assembly unanimously accepted Dawn's challenge to race for the Barrens and passed mandates to preserve the Sign of Tamar and to honour Empress Britta's memorial. Isaac of the Silent Tide was appointed Speaker of the Highborn Assembly.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc priests sent Bloodcrow Udoo to Ossium, reassured the neighbours of the Illarawm, rallied Skarsind's settlers and marked 60 years since Thrace's rebellion. Other assemblies sent orc remains and black lotus potions to the nation, funded mithril for Ethengraw's Armoury, and called for orcs to be admitted to the virtue assemblies.
n.Jotun: The Marches, backed by Wintermark and Navarr mandates and a virtue fund reward for captains to map the territory, prepared a raid on Skallahn. Wintermark priests rejected Jotun honour and Blood on the Snow's bargain, and the Marches urged Mournwold orcs to heed ancestors who did not fight.
n.Navarr: Navarr priests invited the Sand Fishers to walk the trods, sent aid for the Marcher strike against the Jotun and urged Navarr guides to help the Varushkan wardens in Ossium. Harwyn Eternal was appointed Voice of Barbs and vindicated over the Arhallogen deal.
n.The Brass Coast: A Freeborn mandate urged the people to abandon Feroz, while others called refugees to enlist in a new army and sought a new celebration inspired by Zemress. Santana of the Kohan was condemned for heresy, and Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra was inquisited, vindicated and appointed High Exorcist.
n.The League: A League mandate made Sarvos the City of Masks and averted the doom threatening it, and both the League and Wisdom assemblies backed consecrating the gallery above Holberg's Holmauer Gate to Wisdom. Tassato was urged to root out Hatred, and Leonora van Holberg was appointed Patron of the Pavilion.
n.The Marches: Many Whittlefolk, including Little Mournwold's Margret Steward, were condemned for blasphemy in following Hatred. A Marcher mandate prepared a raid on Skallahn, Bregasland fisherfolk were urged to crew raids on Hordalant, and Friar John of the Mourn replaced the revoked Friar of Honour's Rest.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Yulia was revoked for allegedly helping the Thule enslave Jotun thralls, and a later Varushkan statement clarified that the Thule are not enemies of the Empire.
n.Urizen: Urizeni mandates fostered cooperation with the Grendel in Spiral, urged civil debate rather than armed conflict over Sulemaine i Taziel, and encouraged commerce in Redoubt. An intelligence campaign in Zenith was encouraged, but consecrating the Academy of Arms on Mount Siluri failed for want of true liao.
n.Varushka: Varushkan mandates backed the wardens, wagon raiders and native Ossians in Ossium, and the assembly urged the return of enslaved orcs' remains to Skarsind. It also revoked Yulia as senator for Miekarova, condemned the Cabal of the Green Mother and the Heirs of Terunael, and vindicated Nack over the Iron Helms' merciless assault.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark priests commended Isolde Tempest-Shield's work on a sinecure for the nation's armies, praised the heroes fighting the Jotun in Bregasland, and refused support to those who accepted Blood on the Snow's bargain. A mandate sent aid to the Marcher raid, and Maarit Suvidottir became Inquisitor of Courage.

t.Reikos: A Highguard mandate urged chapters near the Sign of Tamar in Reikos to clear the encroaching forest and commit to preserving the historic sigil.

383YE Winter Solstice interlude.d: The Imperial Guerdon of 350 thrones was shared among units supporting the Fist of the Mountain, Tusks, Valiant Pegasus, Winter Sun, Wolves of War and Protect Hercynia. Selling liao to the Axou now earned a full crown. Trade with Asavea suffered under sanctions. Issyk in Axos opened to Imperial traders but under a penalty, and the Kantor penalty was lifted. Robec was closed by the Iron Confederacy, Jarm imposed double tariffs, and the Commonwealth gave extra goods. National mandates affected Highguard, Dawn, Navarr, Varushka, Wintermark, the Brass Coast and anti-idolatry congregations. Four mandates failed because of the Wisdom assembly and the sword scholars.

n.Dawn: Dawnish congregations gained one liao and two votes until the end of the Spring Equinox 384YE. Highborn statements of principle could now come to their attention, under a Highborn mandate seeking understanding between priests and troubadours.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a failed judgement encouraging citizens to travel to Druj-held Zenith and offer aid there.
n.Grendel: In conquering Feroz, the Grendel claimed the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull. Imperial traders lost the benefit that symbol of Asavean cooperation had given them.
n.Highguard: Highborn could upgrade military units for one less wain of mithril, and their congregations gained liao and votes through closer ties with Dawn. They also lost liao and votes to the call to fight the vallorn, and their businesses lost a rank of production to support purifying Holberg's waters.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark units that raided the Jotun-held Pride of Ikka's Tears were rewarded with a morale bonus.
n.Navarr: Every Navarr herb garden lost two herbs a season for a year to support Good Leaf Gardens in Upwold. Herb gardens and forests in Miaren, Therunin and Hercynia were also fed upon by Tharim after the Conclave accepted his aid.
n.The Brass Coast: After the national assembly backed Efenia i Maristela i Riqueza's mandate urging privateering, Freeborn fleet captains who trade suffer a one-rank production penalty for at least two seasons.
n.The League: Under Rafael Barossa di Tassato's anti-idolatry mandate, congregations in Temeschwar and Tassato gained votes and liao. Highborn businesses, meanwhile, were urged to help purify the cursed waters of Holberg.
n.The Marches: Navarr support created Good Leaf Gardens in Upwold, recognising the Marchers' sacrifice against the vallorn of Liathaven. A mandate encouraging Marcher pilgrims to visit Holberg failed.
n.Urizen: Congregations in Redoubt gained votes and liao for as long as the Synod opposes idolatry. Several rituals were also added to Urizen lore.
n.Varushka: Raskylov's mandate raised Varushkan mine and forest production by one rank until the Spring Equinox 384YE. Congregations in Karsk received four extra votes and two liao for a year.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark units that raided the Pride of Ikka's Tears gained a two-rank effectiveness bonus for two seasons under Rafe's mandate. Hahnmark congregations gained votes and liao.

t.Brocéliande: Although Brocéliande's vallorn had grown quiescent, Highborn congregations were called to keep opposing it. The Conclave also accepted Tharim's aid in defending the territory.
t.Feroz: The Grendel conquerors of Feroz claimed the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull there. Imperial traders lost the advantage it had given them with Asavean merchants.
t.Hahnmark: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao, swelled with pride by the anti-idolatry redesign of Asavean-built buildings.
t.Hercynia: Tharim was permitted to feast on Hercynia's herb gardens and forests, costing each two herbs or resources for the next year. Protect Hercynia was among the opportunities sharing the Guerdon.
t.Holberg: Highborn businesses took a production penalty to support purifying Holberg's waters, fouled by the curse that devastated its gardens. A mandate for Marcher pilgrimage there failed.
t.Karsk: Congregations in Karsk received four extra votes and two liao for a year, then the lesser anti-idolatry bonus thereafter.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the Marchers' sacrifice in fighting the vallorn of Liathaven was the reason Good Leaf Gardens were supported in Upwold.
t.Miaren: Tharim was permitted to feast on Miaren's herb gardens and forests, costing each two herbs or resources for the next year.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod clearly stands against idolatry.
t.Tassato: Congregations in Tassato gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod clearly stands against idolatry.
t.Temeschwar: Congregations in Temeschwar gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod clearly stands against idolatry.
t.Therunin: Tharim was permitted to feast on Therunin's herb gardens and forests, costing each two herbs or resources for the next year.
t.Upwold: Good Leaf Gardens were created in Upwold, paid for by reduced Navarr herb production, in recognition of the Marchers' fight against the vallorn.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: a judgement encouraging citizens to travel to Zenith and offer aid failed because of the Wisdom assembly's intervention.

383YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: The ceding of Ankra, Cinion, Ateri, Morajasse and Afarjasse to the Grendel left Freeborn and Urizeni citizens facing hard choices, while the orcs pressed for trade despite Liberty Pact sanctions. The Wisdom assembly and the sword scholars continued to obstruct Synod mandates, and several failed as a result. Varushka was urged to settle Ossium, and the Imperial Orcs eyed the Barrens. The Thule approached Sealtoq with a proposition, and the Navarr sought to lift Wither the Seed. Sarvos became the City of Masks. The Synod rebuked prejudice against briars. The Dawnish Eastern Sky drove the Druj from Holberg, and vallornspawn ran rampant in Liathaven.

n.Dawn: Dawnish troubadours were offered a chapel and ways to support questing knights, and the Eastern Sky drove the last Druj out of Holberg. Dawn must also decide how to respond to the Imperial Orc claim on the Barrens, which it has long fought over.
n.Druj: The Druj were driven from Ennerlund back into the Mallum, and they are on the back foot in the Forest of Ulnak. They now face an Imperial Orc ambition to take the Barrens, though they still threaten Ossium.
n.Grendel: The Grendel consolidated uncontested control of Feroz and the ceded Spiral regions. Their governors made offers to the remaining Imperial citizens and the Citadel Guard, and their merchants sought trade despite Liberty Pact sanctions.
n.Highguard: Highguard's assembly weighed three memorial opportunities, including a new purpose for Empress Britta's shrine. Its three armies gained the Crusade order, and it shared inspiration with Dawn over freeing the Dark Ranging.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were offered ways to press their claim to the Barrens, and Ossean septs arriving in Skarsind hold the promise of a third army. Their interests also feature in the plight of the freed orcs of Axos.
n.Jotun: The Jotun rebuffed Imperial attempts to retake Sermersuaq, and the arrangement keeping them out of Sealtoq is running out. Heroes may face them through Sentinel Gate conjunctions in Bregasland and Sermersuaq.
n.Navarr: The vates answered the call to find ways of lifting Wither the Seed, which is withering the Navarr of Brocéliande. The nation also faces a chance to end the threat of the Heirs of Terunael once and for all.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn of Afarjasse and Morajasse looked to the Synod on whether to stay, resist or flee Grendel rule. Priests visited the Isle of the Osseini, and the Freeborn Assembly declared solidarity with the sword scholars.
n.The League: Sarvos faced doom as it reinvented itself as the City of Masks. The College of Engineering offered the Chair of the Wolf, and the League was asked how it might further help the Sand Fishers of Holberg.
n.The Marches: Marchers debated what to do about Whittle and the Mournwold thralls, and how to protect the nation from future Imperial curses. A thresher concluded that the Singing Caves raiders were the Alderly feni, who were apparently defeated.
n.Thule: The Thule, who hold the Silver Peaks, abandoned their watchful stance and sent a delegation under a flag of truce to Sealtoq with a proposition for Wintermark.
n.Urizen: Urizeni groups offered rituals for Urizen lore in return for favours, and the Grendel governor of Spiral made offers to the remaining citizens and the faltering Citadel Guard. The Urizen Assembly backed the sword scholars and was given chances to work with the eternals of five realms.
n.Varushka: Varushka's national assembly called for settlers, wagon raiders and wardens to tame underdeveloped Ossium. The civil service surveyed the territory's wealth and its new sinecures, and a Varushkan market was proposed.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark sought more healing herbs through the grimnir's practical proposals, and a trading hall was proposed there. The nation also received a Thule offer at Sealtoq, and its stories hint at a magical horn behind the youthful growth spurts.

t.Astolat: New homes amid Astolat's splendour were offered to the ancient cousins of the Freeborn lands, and strange visions were seen in the night sky over the territory.
t.Bastion: The Basilica of the Little Mother in Bastion was destroyed, a tragedy that gave rise to a sorrowful opportunity for the Synod.
t.Bregasland: A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered heroes the chance to fight the Jotun in Bregasland.
t.Brocéliande: Wither the Seed continued to sap the vallorn while devastating Navarr births in Brocéliande. Ways to lift the curse, support the knights questing against the vallorn and free the Dark Ranging were all set out.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: a curse on Casinea, home of Anvil, was listed among the season's magical events.
t.Feroz: The orcs of the Broken Shore consolidated uncontested control of Feroz, leaving its remaining Freeborn to seek the Synod's guidance. Opportunities arose on the Isle of the Osseini.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are described as on the back foot in the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the people of Hahnmark are named among those relevant to the koboldi building opportunities.
t.Holberg: The Druj were driven out of Holberg and the Sand Fishers there sought ways to leave fear behind. Building opportunities included Holmauer Park and the unclaimed Memorial Orchard.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven remained under Wither the Seed as the Heirs and vallornspawn ran rampant, attacking the few remaining Navarr steadings. Its resources suffered a penalty for a year, and the vallornspawn threaten any army that enters.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the people of Miaren are named among those relevant to the koboldi building opportunities.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the people of Miekarova are named among those relevant to the koboldi building opportunities.
t.Morrow: An opportunity arose to solidify the Urizen Assembly's support for the sword scholars in Morrow.
t.Mournwold: The Silent Bell was sent to investigate the Whittle sect, and Marchers debated the fate of Whittle and the Mournwold thralls. Opportunities were offered to address both.
t.Ossium: A year after joining Varushka, underdeveloped and underpopulated Ossium drew calls for settlers. The civil service catalogued Druj spoils that will become new titles and proposed a port, a barracks-armoury and an extension to the Iron Roads.
t.Reikos: Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra appraised the Sign of Tamar in Reikos and submitted proposals for how the site might be preserved and used.
t.Sarvos: After the Hag Queen's curse shattered every mirror in Sarvos, the city chose reinvention as the City of Masks, though a threatened doom must first be overcome.
t.Semmerholm: A chapel for the troubadours was proposed in Semmerholm, and the Druj unexpectedly delivered a hundred Imperial citizens there, apparently at the Emissary of Mazen's say-so.
t.Sermersuaq: Attempts to retake Sermersuaq from the Jotun failed and the Sealtoq foothold is under threat. The Thule approached with a proposition, and conjunctions offered fights against the Jotun there.
t.Skarsind: Ossean orcs settled across Skarsind and new villages sprang up. Three proud septs held out for more, offering the promise of a third Imperial Orc army.
t.Spiral: With Ankra, Cinion and Ateri ceded, the Grendel governor Mahiri Kaliact invited citizens to stay and offered the Citadel Guard a proposal for its survival.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is tagged as especially interested in the Marcher discussions of Tend to the Flame.
t.Temeschwar: The aura of Mellfort in Temeschwar offered opportunities for reflection, and its people were named among those relevant to the koboldi building offers.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the people of Upwold are named among those relevant to the koboldi building opportunities.
t.Weirwater: The legacy of storytellers and musicians was discussed in Weirwater, and a chapel for the troubadours was proposed.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: a mandate urging citizens to travel to Zenith and offer aid failed because of opposition from the Wisdom assembly and the sword scholars.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: The Dawnish and Highborn assemblies backed efforts to free the Dark Ranging from the vallorn before it recovers its strength.
r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Ceded to the Grendel, Afarjasse's remaining Freeborn looked to the Synod on whether to cooperate, resist or flee.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Corsair families of nearby Shantarim made an offer that may especially appeal to Brass Coast privateers.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Ceded to the Grendel, Morajasse's remaining Freeborn sought the Synod's guidance on how to face their new orc overlords.
r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Eastern Sky drove the Druj out of Ennerlund and rooted out their hidden camps, securing the region by the Solstice.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer Park remained blighted and infested with large rats, and the situation there was among the League's building opportunities.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The feni of Alderly who accepted Agramant's offer of vengeance were identified as the Singing Caves raiders, apparently defeated by Imperial heroes.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: The civil service proposed a barracks-armoury in Nearweald to defend Ossium's new vales.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode's Spring regio, Tamar's Toes and every other mana site vanished when the Garden of Llofir was destroyed, leaving little of value at the Sign of Tamar.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: The Empire's foothold in Sealtoq is running out of time against the Jotun, and a Thule delegation arrived there under a flag of truce.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule who hold the Silver Peaks are no longer content to watch and have made a proposition to Wintermark.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Ceded to the Grendel, Ankra's citizens have two seasons to relocate, or may accept the governor's offer to stay and keep out of her affairs.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Ceded to the Grendel, Ateri's citizens face the choice between relocating within two seasons and staying under Mahiri Kaliact.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Ceded to the Grendel, Cinion's citizens weigh leaving with their possessions against the governor's offer of shared Prosperity if they stay.

383YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: Heroes and magic defeated the Heirs of Terunael in Hercynia and Therunin, leaving them unable to threaten either for a year, but Liathaven suffered badly. In Segura the Jotun lost Anozeseri, while the Grendel took Afarjasse, Morajasse and Moras Rock under the peace treaty. In Bregasland the Jotun were turned back amid the emergence of Mathilda Fisher. In Ulnak the Empire claimed about half of Oerwealt. In Zenith a cautious advance escaped a Druj trap and withdrew to Morrow. In Skarsind the Jotun were repulsed at Clattering Gully but threatened to seal Pakaanan's Pass. Sentinel Gate conjunctions to the Caida, Miresend, the Halls of Lutum and Pakaanan's Pass were identified.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun, Hounds of Glory and Gryphon's Pride led the grim invasion of the Forest of Ulnak alongside Varushka, and a troubadour made the first peaceful contact with local orcs. Dawnish captains also fought in great numbers in Hercynia and Therunin.
n.Druj: The Druj lost around half of Oerwealt in Ulnak to the Empire, but in Zenith they sprang a trap from Proceris and Iteri that forced the Imperial armies back into Morrow. They are also reportedly gathering Urizeni prisoners at the Halls of Lutum.
n.Grendel: Under the peace treaty the Iron Gulls took Afarjasse, Morajasse and Moras Rock, giving the Grendel all of Feroz. Lord Rahab was appointed governor and plans to reopen Oran as a trading port.
n.Highguard: The Valiant Pegasus formed the backbone of the defence of Therunin, and Highborn vigilance foiled a plot to poison the orcs building the Holt of the Oak.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind was invaded through Pakaanan's Pass and the garrison of the Will was slowly pushed back, and Jotun executed many orcs who refused the Choice. Elsewhere the Winter Sun led the advance in Segura and the Summer Storm fought in Bregasland.
n.Jotun: The Jotun had mixed fortunes. They were turned back in Bregasland with heavy losses while backing Mathilda Fisher, and the Lasambrians were driven from Anozeseri. They were repulsed at Clattering Gully but are carving runes to bring down Pakaanan's Pass.
n.Navarr: Navarr captains and vates defended Hercynia and Therunin, defeating the Heirs of Terunael at the cost of lives and production. Liathaven's remaining steadings were badly hit, and suspicion of briars grew. The Black Thorns fought in Segura.
n.The Brass Coast: Segura is being won back from the Lasambrian Jotun, but Feroz passed wholly to the Grendel, its Freeborn largely in bondage. Over fifteen hundred Fire of the South soldiers died defending Skarsind.
n.The League: The Towerjacks and the Wolves of War fought in Zenith, briefly securing spires in Clypion before holding the line against the Druj during the withdrawal to Morrow.
n.The Marches: Four Marcher armies helped turn back the Jotun in Bregasland, with the Strong Reeds flooding Jotun camps. Mathilda Fisher, a claimed heir of an old anti-Imperial household, is now calling Marchers to rise against the Empire.
n.Thule: The Thule at Crow's Keep refused to aid either side in Skarsind, citing their oaths. They offered to raise Spring magic to reduce orc deaths if the Imperial Orcs request it through the Ambassador to Otkodov.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard led the failed attempt to liberate Zenith but rescued many Urizeni during the withdrawal, and several hundred captive sentinels await rescue at the Halls of Lutum. Urizeni traitors of Greenfountain Spire aided the Heirs in Therunin.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe spearheaded the advance into Ulnak, while the Northern Eagle and the merciless Iron Helms fought in Zenith. Varushkan cabalists of the Cabal of the Green Mother aided the Heirs of Terunael.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains and the Blood Cloaks fought with honour in Bregasland. The Sussivari Frost Coven and the Eternal Family's citadel aided defences elsewhere, and the Will helped slow the Jotun in Skarsind.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: its salt mines are where the Grendel threaten to send Freeborn of Feroz in reprisal for attacks.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly, though Lord Rahab plans to reopen Oran to Asavean, Sarcophan and Imperial shipping.
t.Bregasland: Imperial armies stopped the Jotun advance eastward and pushed into Grey Fens, losing nearly four thousand soldiers to perhaps twice as many Jotun. Mathilda Fisher's messengers now reach villages across the territory.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Spears of the Pine and the Northern Eagle came from fighting the Heirs there, and its briars' earlier dreams are recalled.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks set out from Casinea with the Citadel Guard for Zenith.
t.Feroz: The whole territory is now held by the Grendel under Lord Rahab. Citizens in Afarjasse and Morajasse have until the Summer Solstice to leave, while Freeborn elsewhere live under harsh rule.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Four Imperial armies invaded and claimed about half of Oerwealt despite miasma, traps and ghosts. Druj from the citadel of Cassad Ûln slowed them, and a new Druj army is rumoured in the east.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: armies can still reach it through Hercynia if Pakaanan's Pass is lost.
t.Hercynia: Its roused vallorn and Heirs' agents attacked steadings and the Heartwood of the Great Vale, but heroes and magic narrowly saved Treji and defeated the Heirs' plans for at least a year.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg Spring magicians joined the Towerjacks, and the League armies' years fighting the Druj there are noted.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Fishers reportedly lived in its marshes for four centuries, and Hordalanter fishermen are among the Yegarra in Bregasland.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Green Shields marched from Kahraman to Bregasland.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark armies came from Kallavesa, and hunters familiar with its marshes were in demand in Bregasland.
t.Karov: The Fire of the South's great column of Ossium orcs crossed Karov, steering clear of its darker places, with only a handful lost to monsters.
t.Karsk: The refugee column crossed Karsk under Freeborn escort; some vales offered hospitality while others closed their doors.
t.Liathaven: Unopposed, the Heirs likely achieved their aims. Steadings suffered near-catastrophic damage, production is penalised for a year, extra Treasury support is diverted, and vallornspawn infest the territory.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Moras Rock garrison withdrew north into Madruga after surrendering the fortress.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes crossed into Bregasland from Oddmire.
t.Morrow: Imperial armies marched from Morrow into Zenith and withdrew back to it to regroup. Traitors from Greenfountain Spire in Peregro aided the Heirs in Therunin.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: former Mournwold Yegarra, including Steven of Sarcombe, fight with the Jotun in Bregasland and invoke the curses of the Mourn.
t.Ossium: Around eight thousand Ossium orcs left with the Fire of the South for Skarsind, and the invasion of Ulnak was launched from Ossium's eastern borders.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov's word could secure Thule Spring magic for Skarsind.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: it sheltered Zenith refugees and lies beyond the high passes by which freed Halls of Lutum prisoners could escape.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Druj miasma there is recalled as a precedent for Ulnak.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: Lasambrian orcs are camped near its border, and the Black Thorns aim to drive them back into it.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War marched from Sarvos to Zenith.
t.Segura: The Black Thorns, Winter Sun and Red Wind Corsairs drove the Lasambrian Jotun from Anozeseri and are about halfway to expelling them. The orcs now hold Anduz and dig at the Caida.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: it is not named, though Dawn's earlier crossing of the Semmerlak by the Golden Causeway is recalled.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun launched their Skarsind attack from East Floes. If they seal Pakaanan's Pass, Imperial armies will be unable to reach Sermersuaq from Skarsind without Thule permission.
t.Skarsind: About fifteen thousand Jotun invaded and executed many orcs who refused the Choice. They were repulsed at Clattering Gully but are close to taking Pakaanan's Pass, while Ossium emigrants camp near Gildenheim.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Halls of Lutum were built to watch the borders with Redoubt and Spiral.
t.Tathar: Mentioned in passing: its salt mines are where resisting Freeborn of Feroz may be sent.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's earlier crossing of it on the Golden Causeway is recalled.
t.Therunin: The Valiant Pegasus, captains, Great Forest Orcs and magic defeated the Heirs and Greenfountain traitors. The Thimble was saved at great cost, but its output is halved and all production is reduced for a season.
t.Zenith: Over thirty thousand Imperial troops entered but withdrew after narrowly escaping a Druj encirclement, losing about fifteen hundred soldiers.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Imperial forces struck deep into Grey Fens and are just short of halfway to pushing the Jotun out.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: It remains under Jotun control. Mathilda Fisher has raised her call from Fisher's Rock, and a conjunction offers a strike on the Yegarra near Miresend.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The Jotun were forced out. Locals helped the Strong Reeds open sluice gates to flood enemy camps under Sussivari mist-fortifications.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The Strong Reeds and the Bounders intercepted Jotun incursions here and forced the orcs to give up their positions.
r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Ceded to the Iron Gulls, who occupy the Spice Gardens worked by orc slaves; citizens may leave until the Summer Solstice.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Its Freeborn remain effectively slaves of the Grendel, with orc sentinels punishing any who try to flee.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Its Freeborn remain in Grendel bondage and are barred from fleeing north or west.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Ceded to the Iron Gulls, who took over the newly completed Moras Rock; citizens may leave until the Summer Solstice.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Its Freeborn stay under Grendel control while Lord Rahab meets Asavean envoys at Oran and plans to reopen its port.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt: The haunted, cursed Trackless Forest of the last Woodcreeper villages is half to three-fifths in Imperial hands, despite resistance from the Cassad Ûln garrison.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: The vallorn heart here was roused by the Heirs, and ettercaps and vallornspawn spilled out to attack the rest of Hercynia.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: The Navarr here faced Heirs' agents rather than vallornspawn, aided by the Eternal Family's citadel of white stone and black ice; Jotun scouts also probed the area.
r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: The Voice of the Quiet Forest raised a magical fortress from its woodlands to help contain the vallornspawn.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: Spring magic twined a woodland fortress here as the territory resisted the vallorn's incursion.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes crossed out of Oddmire into Bregasland.
r.Morrow/Caeli: Five Imperial armies marched down its passes beneath the Three Watchers into Zenith, and later withdrew back through them.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Traitorous magicians and sentinels of Greenfountain Spire in Peregro aided the Heirs of Terunael in Therunin.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: Jonathan Thresher of Alderly is listed among the defenders of Hercynia.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Mentioned in passing: the four armies crossed its far borders to invade Ulnak.
r.Segura/Anozeseri: The Lasambrian Jotun lost their foothold here and fell back towards Anduzjasse.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Scouts found a large orc force in the hills to its south, digging at the Caida battleground, now reachable by a Sentinel Gate conjunction.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Two Jotun armies and allied Yegarra surged from East Floes through Pakaanan's Pass into Skarsind.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: the only other army route from Skarsind runs through Crow's Ridge into the Silver Peaks, unlikely to be opened by the Thule.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: The Thule garrison at Crow's Keep stayed neutral, and its pass is now the only alternative route to Sermersuaq.
r.Skarsind/Estermark: Jotun warbands raided as far as Estermark.
r.Skarsind/Gildermark: Jotun warbands raided here. The Fire of the South arrived with Ossium emigrants, now camped outside Gildenheim, in time to defend Clattering Gully.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The Jotun are a little shy of halfway to conquering it and are carving runes to bring down the mountains, which a Sentinel Gate conjunction may let heroes stop.
r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: The Will based here blunted the Jotun attacks, though its garrison was pushed back towards the Glens and faced probing strikes.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: The Sussivari Frost Coven's living mist shielded defenders here as marsh beasts attacked its steadings.
r.Therunin/Eastring: The Voice of the Quiet Forest raised a wooden fastness here, though its steadings were still attacked.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Spore-crazed dire beetles and other abominations poured from this vallorn region as the Heirs sought to overrun Therunin.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Great Forest Orcs and the Spears of the Pine defended their homes, and a plot to poison the builders of the Holt of the Oak was foiled.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Imperial Orc patrols foiled a ritual to breach Peakedge Stead's gates, protecting its hospital, though vallornspawn still assailed its walls.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Its vallorn abominations were roused by the Heirs and the Greenfountain traitors in their attempt to overrun the territory.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Imperial armies briefly reclaimed half a dozen spires before withdrawing. A conjunction now offers a chance to destroy its miasma pillars and free prisoners at the Halls of Lutum.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Imperial scouts vanished here, and a second massive Druj force emerged from Iteri to strike the Imperial flank.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The Druj roused its dark, twisted forests with magic to protect their conquest.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Druj quickened its marshes and hid a huge army in a western vale, which surged out against the Imperial eastern flank.

A health to the company.d: The College of Engineering, using improved versions of Frederick di Sarvos's sketches, needed only a Senate motion to expand. If League Senators began a commission of at least 30 wains in each of Sarvos, Tassato, Temeschwar and Holberg by the Winter Solstice 384YE, a Chair of the Wolf, chosen by Tally of the Votes, could commit the Guild of Engineers to League construction without using up Imperial commissions. In Holmauer Park the waters were being cleansed, and a Loyalty mandate could make the Memorial Garden a shrine. Georgie's House could expand for 23 crowns, which the Senate approved. Mellfort's sorrow-easing aura could support either a Synod shrine or the Emerald Magpie Guild's Palace of Rest, but not both.

n.Highguard: The Highborn National Assembly upheld Lina of Felix's Watch's mandate urging Highborn business owners to cleanse the befouled waters of Holmauer, and that work was well underway.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is listed among the places whose citizens know the trouble rats cause, as demand grows for Holberg's trained ratters.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the cities troubled by rats, where interest in dogs from Georgie's House was growing.
n.The League: The League was challenged to begin an impressive commission in each of its four cities by Winter 384YE to win the Chair of the Wolf and the services of the Guild of Engineers. It also faced choices over Holmauer Park and Mellfort, and saw the Senate approve the expansion of Georgie's House.
n.The Marches: Aureliana di Sarvos's statement honoured the untouched Marcher apple grove in Holmauer Park as a symbol of Marcher Loyalty, though the Marcher Assembly's own pilgrimage mandate was not enacted. A Loyalty mandate could now make the Memorial Garden of General Flowers a shrine.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Gildenheim is listed among the cities all too aware of rats, as demand for Holberg's trained ratters spreads.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is named among the places where rats are a fact of urban life and interest in Georgie's House dogs was growing.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Gildenheim is named among the cities troubled by rats that were taking an interest in Holberg's ratters.
t.Holberg: The College of Engineering in Holberg sought Senate permission to expand, and a commission begun in the city would count towards the Chair of the Wolf challenge. The Senate approved the expansion of Georgie's House kennels, which was set to bring its Custodian an additional 100 rings each season.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the cities whose citizens know the problem of rats and were looking to Holberg's kennels.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Meade is listed among the cities where rats are a problem and demand for Georgie's House ratters was growing.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos was one of the four cities needing an impressive commission for the Chair of the Wolf, and the College suggested refurbishing Capodomus Cathedral, which some faculty consider long overdue.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is named among the places plagued by rats, where Holberg-trained ratters were becoming sought after.
t.Tassato: Tassato needed an impressive commission within its walls for the Chair of the Wolf challenge. The Imperial Consulate qualified, but the Tagliano market and the Mestran Hills Mutual Association, built outside the walls, did not.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar needed a qualifying commission for the Chair of the Wolf challenge, and the College said turning Ratibor's Gate or the Red Tower into a shrine blessed with true liao would count. Mellfort's aura offered a choice between a Synod shrine and a Palace of Rest.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Pavilion was inspiring efforts to reclaim the cursed Holmauer Park and its waters were being cleansed, but the Blood Orchard, Sculpture Garden and Duelling Fields opportunities were due to lapse after the Winter Solstice. The Duelling Field Menhirs would count towards the College's challenge, and the Memorial Garden could become a Loyalty shrine.
r.Temeschwar/Locul: At Mellfort, the Synod judged the aura of a cavern beneath the mountain to be neither virtuous nor unvirtuous but able to ease sorrow. It could become either a shrine with a Synod title or the Emerald Magpie Guild's Palace of Rest, but not both, and neither opportunity was time-limited.

A horn resounding.d: Believing Wintermark faced its darkest hour, Kirsa and Summer magicians at Rundhal magnified the horn with a ritual. It gave a single note and broke, and no Summer heroes appeared. Later, children under sixteen experienced month-long Summer-driven growth spurts that aged them mentally and physically, prompting emergency citizenship tests. The Seers of the Barren Tree in Woodbury claimed many past heroes had been reborn, and offered a dose of true liao for a young citizen chosen by the Gatekeepers, who duly selected one. The herald Elioe collected children's accounts for the Great Library, and many eternals, even the enemy Agramant, offered boons to Summer Children.

n.Highguard: The Highborn chapter of the Seers of the Barren Tree claimed the Summer Children proved great heroes were being reborn, and supplied a dose of true liao for a young citizen chosen by the Gatekeepers.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Kirsa cites the orcs holding Skarsind as a sign of Wintermark's darkest hour.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Kirsa cites the Jotun holding the ice floes as part of Wintermark's plight.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the legendary Marjatta of the Three Spears is said to have defeated Agramant's champion Jedza Toothunger in the forests of Hercynia.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Marjatta of the Three Spears is remembered as Field Marshal at the Battle of the Golden Groves during the conquest of Karsk.
n.Wintermark: A Wintermark scop judged her nation, reduced to half of what it once was, to be at its darkest hour and spent its long-guarded Horn of Hope, which shattered as it sounded.

t.Bastion: The Seers of the Barren Tree, founded in Bastion in 317YE, had kept a dose of true liao in their chapter house there awaiting this moment.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Tarsus of Casinea, whose past-life vision inspired the Seers, lived out his days tending fruit trees in his chapter house there.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is home to Kirsa Wordsmith and the line of scops who guarded the Horn of Hope for over a century.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the forests of Hercynia are where Marjatta of the Three Spears is said to have defeated Jedza Toothunger.
t.Kallavesa: At Rundhal in Kallavesa a coven of Summer magicians helped Kirsa perform the Solstice ritual before she sounded and shattered the horn.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Marjatta served as Field Marshal at the Battle of the Golden Groves in the conquest of Karsk.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Marjatta is said to have destroyed the Crimson Artok in the mountains above Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the orcs holding Skarsind is cited by Kirsa as evidence of Wintermark's darkest hour.

r.Bastion/Woodbury: Woodbury houses the Seers of the Barren Tree's chapter house, from which their stored true liao will go to a young citizen chosen by the Gatekeepers.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Wood Heath is the home of Kirsa Wordsmith, the scop who bore and sounded the Horn of Hope.

Across the Abyss.d: Freed from Druj slavery and settled in Misericorde, the Sand Fishers were transformed by the Imperial victory and by Bartimaeus of the Shattered Tower's Prosperity mandate. They came to believe the Way had beaten the Druj miasma. They asked for Imperial education and access to Holberg University, for Imperial lore through the Conclave, and for a Senate appraisal of Holberg's forests. They also arranged to trade herbs for mithril or weirwood at the planned Misericorde Market, saying it was 'for next time'. Troubled by the tenet to despise those who take without giving, they asked what they could do for the Empire. The Synod raised statements of advice, and the Senate raised Holberg's funding to support their study at the university.

n.Druj: The Druj risked everything on an attack into Holberg to punish the Sand Fishers' 'rebellion', but Imperial heroes intercepted them and their armies fled back into the Barrens. Their former slaves now say their ancestors urge them to wipe out every last Druj.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Eliza recalls reading that Imperial Orcs often hear conflicting things from their ancestors, which proves a poor guide to the Sand Fishers.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a recent misunderstanding in Therunin is cited as an example of the risks of sharing Imperial lore with outsiders.
n.The League: Holberg's people were urged to trade fairly with the Sand Fishers and did so. The territory's merchants and the coming Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market stood to gain herb trades for mithril or weirwood, and Holberg University was opened to the orcs through extra Senate funding.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's free basic education for citizens is described as a legacy of Urizen joining the Empire.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers were first encountered when Imperial armies invaded Ossium, the land they fled.

t.Holberg: The Druj invasion of Holberg was repelled. The Sand Fishers living there grew in Prosperity and Ambition, and they won Senate funding, raised through Holberg's upkeep, to study at Holberg University. A planned market there is set to trade their herbs for mithril and weirwood.
t.Ossium: Ossium was where the Sand Fishers were enslaved and brutalised by the Druj for decades and where the Druj kept herbal places of study. The Druj took heavy losses there, and its defeat is held up as proof that their hoarding failed them.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: a recent misunderstanding in Therunin is cited as a warning about how shared ritual lore might be used unexpectedly.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers' new home in the forests of Misericorde was the Druj army's target before it was stopped. The orcs there now consecrate round houses, await the Misericorde Market and are eager to develop the largely undeveloped land.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Mentioned in passing: the forests of Utterlund are noted as having only sporadic farms and herb gardens, as part of the case for an appraisal of Holberg's wilds.

All at sea.d: Asavea is hosting a summit that excludes the Liberty Pact, and Jarm has closed its ports to Imperial captains. The Alivetti estates in Sarvos were ceded to the Sarcophan Vandersaar, who are building an enclave there and offering land for a Temple of the Way in the Delves. Asavean exiles in Trajadoz are sending envoys to Anvil. Smuggling rings into Faraden lands were confirmed in Kahraman and Segura. A Sentinel Gate conjunction allows a meeting with the Great Forest Orcs. The Thule released almost all remaining Imperial slaves. At the Solstice the magistrates were sent to investigate the smuggling, and the College of Maykop and Lyceum Schloss were commissioned.

n.Dawn: The Free Folk exiles were invited by troubadours to discuss moving to Dawn, and Dawnish envoys could meet the Great Forest Orcs, who hold enduring grudges against Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Axou scouts aided the Imperial spy network completed in the Druj-held marshes of Sarangrave.
n.Grendel: Now treated as foreigners, the Grendel hold the Temple of the Black Bull in Feroz and let Asavean merchants dock there, drawing to themselves the goodwill Imperial fleets once enjoyed. They are also rumoured to be sending a delegation to the Nemoria gathering.
n.Highguard: Highborn ambassadors handle Jarm and Sumaah, while Necropolis saw an expanded Sarcophan herb warehouse, a dispute over the Black Sails Quay, and a Free Folk pilgrimage to Empress Richilde's tomb.
n.Imperial Orcs: Chainbreaker Pakt serves as Ambassador to Asavea, and the orc-controlled Steel Fist Bourse seat permanently gains 4 extra rings of ilium each season from the new Sarcophan enclave.
n.Jotun: The Jotun hold the Faraden embassy, smuggled goods flow into their territory of Reinos, and a Thule delegation was coming to Anvil to propose an alliance with Wintermark against them.
n.Navarr: Their Great Forest Orc allies will only meet through a delegation that includes a Navarr, and twenty Navarr artisans taken by the Thule at Treji were returned home.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn host Asavean exiles at Trajadoz and were found to be running smuggling rings into Faraden lands. Rival Synod mandates could oppose or back the smugglers, and at the Solstice the magistrates were sent to investigate.
n.The League: The ruined Alivetti estates in Sarvos were ceded to the Sarcophan for a trading enclave, Empress Giselle's tomb became a guided landmark, and League ambassadors handle the Commonwealth and Faraden.
n.Thule: The Thule released what they say are all their remaining Imperial slaves under the Sungold treaty, apparently put down trouble in Sküld, and planned to send envoys to Wintermark about an alliance against the Jotun.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Tarquinius Ankarien is Ambassador to Axos, and Commonwealth magicians are studying at the Lyceum. The Redoubt senator's motion for the Elosian docks has made no progress.
n.Varushka: Commonwealth zauberer visited the Icy Crag in Miekarova, and groups of freed Imperial slaves were handed over in Miekarova and at Ivarsgard in Karsk.
n.Wintermark: A Thule delegation was coming to court Wintermark for an alliance against the Jotun, Thanmir Hrafnar is Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves, and about a dozen Winterfolk artisans remain held by the Thule.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the bay is not named directly, though the page covers the overseas trade and diplomacy carried by the Empire's southern sea routes.
t.Feroz: The Temple of the Black Bull still stands under Grendel control, and Asavean merchants dock there by order of the Salt Lords. The Wisdom Assembly wanted the temple destroyed, but the Empire cannot do so.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: twenty Navarr artisans taken during the Thule conquest of Treji in Hercynia were among the freed slaves.
t.Kahraman: Several smuggling rings were found moving goods from Kahraman into Faraden lands, with one route running on into the Marches. One proposed mandate would give its businesses extra ingots.
t.Karsk: One of three large groups of freed Imperial slaves was delivered by the Thule to Ivarsgard in Karsk.
t.Madruga: The empty town of Trajadoz now houses the Marracossan and Free Folk exiles from Asavea, who are seeking recognition of their settlement and a temple to their gods.
t.Miekarova: A Commonwealth professor and students studied Summer lore at the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and a group of freed Imperial slaves was delivered here.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: a copy of the Empire's map of the mountains was shared with Axos under the treaty.
t.Necropolis: The Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Crown's Quay was expanded, Axou traders petitioned to change how the Black Sails Quaymaster is appointed, and Free Folk pilgrims decorated Empress Richilde's tomb.
t.Otkodov: The Thule homeland sent back almost all remaining Imperial slaves across its border, and there was apparently conflict in Sküld that the Thule appear to have contained.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the senator of Redoubt raised a motion to build the Elosian docks, but no progress has been made.
t.Reinos: Goods smuggled from the Brass Coast pass into the Lasambrain Hills of Reinos, west of the Freeborn border.
t.Sarangrave: Axou scouts and Toxatai supported the Imperial spy network completed in the marshes and will share any intelligence it gathers, including a possible map.
t.Sarvos: The Alivetti estates were ceded to the Sarcophan Vandersaar, who are raising an enclave there and giving guided tours of Empress Giselle's ruined tomb. Asavean backers of the Cavabiance Docks fear being forced to stop trading.
t.Segura: Smuggling rings operate here despite the war with the Jotun, and members of the Hand of Dumon were executed crossing from Segura into the Confederacy. One proposed mandate would give its businesses extra ingots.
t.Skarsind: One of three groups of freed Imperial slaves was delivered here, and visiting Thule merchants brought vague word of trouble in Sküld.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the situation in Grendel-held Spiral is covered in a separate wind of fortune.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest Orcs and their Navarr neighbours came through the clash with the Heirs of Terunael largely unscathed, the Holt of the Oak was completed, and the new senator is expected to lead the delegation through the Sentinel Gate.

r.Otkodov/Sküld: Rumours tell of conflict here, possibly involving the vallorn around the lost city of Emrys, which the Thule appear to have suppressed.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: A Sentinel Gate conjunction at 2pm on the Sunday lets six people reach the Chief's Contemplation Glade to meet Chief Vallack and the elders, now guarded by the completed Holt of the Oak.

All lift together.d: Pahkina's statement of principle passed 223-0 at the Autumn Equinox 383YE. It confused many, as few outside Anvil knew of Asny's role as 'head healer'. The healers offered four routes. Existing herb sinecures in Hahnmark could become annual titles with a duty to supply Wintermark's heroes, gaining a ministry. The Healing House of Wittal Grove could be rebuilt in Kallavesa (56 wains of weirwood, 112 crowns) with a Grimnir of Wittal Grove title. An Assembly mandate could let warriors work for herbs. Hufi's Garden near Masi could be commissioned as a Woundbinder of the Mark sinecure. The Senate commissioned the Healing House, but its motion had significant problems.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: raids against the Druj in the Mallum are named as one way warriors could earn herbs if the proposed Wintermark mandate were enacted.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn of Liathaven, which the Jotun then held, is named as a place warriors might raid for herbs under the proposed mandate.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn of Hercynia is named as a place warriors might raid for herbs under the proposed mandate.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's grimnir and healers rallied to the Assembly's call. They offered to sell spare herbs to titles that serve the nation's heroes and proposed new great works, titles and a mandate. The Senate commissioned the Healing House of Wittal Grove, though the motion ran into legal trouble.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's existing herb sinecures and Freya's Garden were pointed to as resources. The sinecures could be amended into annual titles obliged to supply Wintermark's warriors and able to buy herbs.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn is listed as somewhere military units might raid for herbs if the Wintermark mandate were enacted.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa was singled out by the Assembly's call. Proposals followed for the Healing House of Wittal Grove, which would add a shared bounty of 90 herbs a season to Wintermark herb gardens there, and for Hufi's Garden near Masi. The Senate commissioned the Healing House at the Winter Solstice.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn is listed as somewhere military units might raid for herbs if the Wintermark mandate were enacted.

r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: Kalpamark hosts the hot-spring Garden of Falling Snow and the Master Apothecary's Garden. The page suggests the Gatekeeper of Falling Snow title could be reshaped to serve Wintermark's warriors, as the Master Apothecary already does.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The overgrown, Spring-touched ruins of Hufi Villesdottir's estate near Masi were proposed as Hufi's Garden. This sinecure, for a Woundbinder of the Mark, would cost 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns, and its commissioning is not recorded here.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Elina of Redleaf's Hall proposed rebuilding Sigrid the Redleaf's old Healing House at Wittal Grove under a Grimnir of Wittal Grove. The Senate commissioned it at the Winter Solstice, but the Constitutional Court is resolving problems with the motion.

An unexpected alignment.d: With the Empire clinging to Sealtoq and the year-long Jotun truce there nearly expired, the Thule, whose own peace with the Jotun had lapsed, offered the Talons of the Wind, the Banner of the Rime Hound and the Earthquake Drummers for up to a year. Their conditions were that Imperial armies always outnumber Thule armies, that the campaign be pursued seriously, that no territory-wide slaughter curses be used, and that their Rivers of Life curse go unhindered. The price was one region per army, chosen from Skogei Glens, Miechernya, Branoc or the Webwood, or alternatively Opascari or Brez in place of three. They also wanted the right to take captured orc thralls to Otkodov as slaves. An envoy would negotiate at Anvil.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Thule named the Skogei Glens in Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, as one of the regions they would accept as payment. Their demand to enslave captured orc thralls also bore directly on orcish people.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were the intended target of a joint Imperial and Thule campaign to drive them from Sermersuaq. Their truce over Sealtoq was nearly at an end, and the Thule rebuffed their envoys' attempts to extend their own peace.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the deaths of Jotun thralls in the Mournwold were cited as the reason Jotun diplomacy had failed, and the Thule cited them again as grounds for their ban on slaughter curses.
n.Thule: Emboldened by their success in Ossium and urged on by the Eternal Dragons, the Thule offered three armies against the Jotun. They sought new Imperial regions and orc slaves as their price, and the Senate ultimately ratified a treaty securing their aid.
n.Varushka: Most of the regions the Thule demanded were Varushkan, including Miechernya, Branoc, the Webwood, and the prized Opascari and Brez. These could be ceded or simply left for Thule armies to conquer.
n.Wintermark: The offer gave Wintermark a chance to retake the Suaq homeland of Sermersuaq with Thule help. When told the regions demanded were not Wintermark's, Hoosfa Mek shrugged and treated that as Wintermark's problem to solve.

t.Karsk: Karsk's region of Branoc was one of the regions the Thule would accept as payment for each army they committed.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's region of Miechernya was offered as one possible region the Thule would take in exchange for an army.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the killing of Jotun thralls in the Mournwold was cited as the source of continuing Jotun hostility and of the Thule's refusal to tolerate slaughter curses.
t.Ossium: The Thule called their invasion of Ossium a success that had whetted their appetite for conquest. The Webwood in Ossium was among the regions they would accept as payment.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov was named as the beneficiary of Thule conquest. Captured orc thralls would be taken there as slaves to serve the Dragons.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was the focus of the proposed year-long joint campaign to reconquer the territory from the Jotun. The Thule planned to cast Rivers of Life over it and forbade territory-wide slaughter curses there.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind's Skogei Glens was listed among the regions the Thule would accept in return for committing an army.
t.Volodmartz: The Thule would accept either Opascari or Brez in Volodmartz as worth three regions, because of the valuable bourse resources each holds.

r.Karsk/Branoc: Branoc was one of the four regions the Thule named as acceptable payment of one region per army.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Miechernya was named as an acceptable region for the Thule to receive, whether by cession or by unopposed conquest.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Webwood was listed among the regions the Thule would take as the price of one army's support.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Mentioned in passing: the Thule delegation travelled to Sealtoq through the Jotun-controlled East Floes.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Sealtoq was the Empire's last foothold in Sermersuaq, and the Jotun's year-long agreement not to fight there was nearly over. It was here that the Thule delegation arrived under a white flag to make its offer.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule, who had held and magically fortified the Silver Peaks since 379YE, abandoned their silent watch. They insisted that no slaughter curses endanger the people of the Silver Peaks.
r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: The Skogei Glens were one of the regions the Thule would accept in exchange for an army.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: Brez, home of the Granites of Veltsgorsk, was offered as an alternative payment worth three regions.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: Opascari, with its Hunt of Alderei the Fair, was offered as an alternative payment worth three regions.

Apples from a tree.d: Suaq icewalker Artja Fivefeet proposed the Kauppahall, a twinned trading hall in Valashal costing 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, with a Wintermark title, the Talon of Kauppahall, to buy white granite and some ilium. Varushkan boyars under Oksana Lyava Pinavora proposed enlarging Korotny's docks for 18 wains of white granite and 36 crowns, creating a Harbour Master of Semmerlak to buy weirwood and ilium. Each project would end public auction supply of a resource. The Senate commissioned the Kauppahall, though the appointment method it named was unconstitutional, and the Parador of Dust. The Blackfield Market lapsed. The Korotny opportunity remains until Summer 384YE. Bartimaeus then enacted a Prosperity mandate for Redoubt.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish declined to build the Star Metal Market in Lacre, which prompted the Varushkan boyars' alternative plan, and Dawn is named as a trading partner of Korotny.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is named as one of the partners in Korotny's substantial trade across the Semmerlak.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the ever-present threat of the Thule is described as the only check on Korotny's ambitions.
n.Urizen: After the Solstice, Bartimaeus of the Prosperity Assembly enacted a mandate urging the citizens of Redoubt to seek ways to increase their prosperity, which could lead to a new commercial opportunity there.
n.Varushka: Wealthy Varushkan boyars led by Oksana Lyava Pinavora proposed enlarging the Korotny docks, which would create a Harbour Master of Semmerlak chosen by Varushkan mine and forest owners. The Senate did not commission it, but the opportunity remains until the end of the Summer Solstice 384YE.
n.Wintermark: The Senate commissioned the Kauppahall in Valashal, which would give Wintermark a national title, the Talon of Kauppahall, to buy white granite and ilium. However, the appointment method the Senators named was unconstitutional; the civil service had advised a tally of votes among Wintermark military unit leaders.

t.Hahnmark: The Kauppahall, a rune-shaped twinned trading hall at Valashal, was commissioned to draw merchants from southern Hahnmark and northern Kallavesa and trade stone and ilium from the nearby hills.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is noted as a partner in Korotny's lake-trade on the Semmerlak.
t.Karov: A plan was put forward to enlarge Korotny's docks on the Semmerlak, making them the outlet for weirwood and lake ilium. It was not commissioned this season, but it remains available until the end of the Summer Solstice 384YE.
t.Redoubt: Following the Solstice, Bartimaeus enacted a Prosperity mandate encouraging Redoubt's citizens to seek new ways to increase their prosperity, which could give rise to a commercial opportunity at the next summit.

r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: Valashal, built on the site of the razed and supposedly cursed Runehall, is to gain the commissioned Kauppahall, a trading hall meant to enrich Valasmark through trade in white granite and ilium from the surrounding hills.

Between wind and water.d: The Thorns of a Rose, a weaver cabal in Culwich, prepared three bondrings for Claude Cutter, Roland Singer and Tristaine Tiller, to be hallowed by Dawnish priests. Earl Mathilde Courcillon offered to rebuild a chapel in Ferrond near Elayne Silverlark's empty tomb, which would create the Troubadour of Auvanne. Earl deGramont proposed Greenwood Manor and an expanded Greenforest Fair at Racqueen in Elvette, creating the Knight of the Greenwood and the Reeve of Greenforest Fair. Lady Eleanor Novarion drafted a mandate inviting Marracossan refugees in Trajadoz to the House of the Proffered Hand, and proposed it at the Winter Solstice. The Senate did not support Greenwood Manor, but it was later built under an Imperial Wayleave and both titles became active.

n.Dawn: Dawn's troubadours, knights and priests were offered several opportunities: bondrings for its prize-winning storytellers, a chapel and the Troubadour of Auvanne title, Greenwood Manor with titles for both a noble and a yeofolk, and a mandate to draw Asavean followers of the Way into Dawnish life.
n.Navarr: Navarr thorns had found succour at the deGramont estate during the struggle against the Heirs of Terunael, and Navarr stridings leaving Brocéliande regularly stop at Racqueen, where an expanded fair was expected to draw still more of their traffic.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Marracossan refugees whom Dawn hoped to invite to Astolat were then living in Trajadoz in Madruga.

t.Astolat: The House of the Proffered Hand in Astolat, overseen by Lady Eleanor Novarion, was proposed as the new home for Marracossan refugees who follow the Way, with any resulting problems falling to her to resolve.
t.Brocéliande: The roused vallorn of Brocéliande was the main target of the proposed Greenwood Manor, which was eventually built to encourage Dawnish knights to quest against it and to trade the treasures recovered from its ruins.
t.Madruga: A community of Marracossan former slaves living in Trajadoz was the subject of a proposed Dawnish mandate to persuade them to resettle at the House of the Proffered Hand.
t.Semmerholm: Two Semmerholm noble houses made offers: Earl Mathilde Courcillon a troubadours' chapel in Ferrond, and Earl deGramont Greenwood Manor and an expanded Greenforest Fair in Elvette, the latter eventually completed.
t.Weirwater: The Thorns of a Rose, a weaver cabal from Culwich led by Sibylla, offered three bondrings to Dawn's prize-winning storytellers and promised a yearly Fireglass to any troubadour who holds the Troubadour of Auvanne title.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Mentioned in passing: the in-character tale of a poisoned Argent Dawn knight and her retainer takes place in a storm on the edge of Boar's Dell.
r.Semmerholm/Elvette: The deGramont estate near Racqueen in Elvette was the site of the proposed Greenwood Manor and expanded Greenforest Fair, which were later built under an Imperial Wayleave.
r.Semmerholm/Ferrond: Earl Mathilde Courcillon offered to rebuild her chapel in Ferrond, overlooking Endric's Hill and Elayne Silverlark's empty tomb, as a ministry and venue for the Troubadour of Auvanne; the page records no outcome for this offer.

Beyond the light.d: Ossium remained under-developed, underpopulated and under threat from lingering Druj, while bandits and roused wolves preyed on settlers crossing Karsk. Military units could take one of three independent actions. Wagon raiding meant fighting Druj and seizing caches. Sellswords would protect settlers and vales. Wardens would explore the territory and contact isolated humans and non-Druj orcs. The combined strength committed would decide overall success, and the strongest action would shape the Spring opportunities. Each action also risked trouble: with the eternal Arhallogen, with the bandits of Karsk, or with the Thule. Several mandates were enacted to back all three approaches, including Varushkan, Imperial Orc, Dawnish and Navarr ones.

n.Dawn: Dawn's armies had done most of the fighting to conquer Ossium. Pelleas Montrose enacted the mandate urging Dawnish knights-errant and questing knights to join the wagon raiders against the Druj, which promised Dawn a Spring opportunity to tackle the under threat problem if the effort succeeded.
n.Druj: Druj guerrillas, holdfasts and the Arhallogen-linked temple in the Webwood were the targets of the wagon raiders and their allies, and the Druj still threatened to return through Ossium's eastern forests.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skywise Tulva's statement of principle was followed by Bloodcrow Udoo enacting a mandate sending Imperial Orc preachers to reach out to Ossium's remaining orcs and support the wardens. This promised an opportunity to deal with the territory's independent orcs.
n.Navarr: Nathair Autumngale enacted a Navarr mandate encouraging guides to help Varushkan wardens reach isolated settlements in Ossium, adding its strength to the wardens' action on top of the Varushkan support.
n.The League: The League had already given a home in Holberg to former Druj-ruled orcs. Its assembly was offered a mandate to send mercenaries and towerjacks to support the settlers, though the page does not record it being enacted.
n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov held Bonewood and still resented being refused the chance to recruit Ossium's orcs. Explorers straying into their lands risked giving them grounds to seek reparations from the Empire.
n.Varushka: Varushka's assembly drove the effort to secure its new territory. Varushkan mandates were enacted backing wagon raiders, wardens, and sellswords who would seek out former Druj slaves to found new vales.
