Meanwhile the boyar of Isember planned to visit Anvil amid concerns over banditry in Karsk.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: cited as the place where Arhallogen secured Druj warriors to aid the Navarr during recent troubles.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: noted as the territory Dawn's armies were invading while the Dawnish knights were urged to fight in Ossium.
t.Holberg: The League had offered Holberg as a new home to the Sand Fishers of Bittershore, with the Senate ceding a region of it to these former Druj subjects.
t.Karsk: Bandits were preying on settlers and supply wagons heading for Ossium, and the violence had stirred up undead and monstrous wolves along the roads. Supporting the settlers risked making the Karsk bandits bolder, while the boyar of Isember sought talks over concerns about his vale.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is not named directly on the page.
t.Ossium: Ossium was the focus of the opportunity, under-developed, underpopulated and under threat from the Druj. A major victory could strip one of these qualities from a region, and success would bring further Spring opportunities.
t.Otkodov: The Thule of Otkodov, whose ambassador was Yevgeni Katzev, could seek reparations if Imperial adventurers trespassed into their lands in Ossium.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: many former orc subjects of the Druj had left Ossium to seek new homes in Skarsind.

r.Ossium/Bittershore: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers of Bittershore had been offered a new home in Holberg by the League.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Thule held Bonewood, and enthusiastic wardens or adventurers risked straying into it, prompting delicate negotiations and possible demands for reparations.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: If the wardens' action led a major victory, the Drownbark Forest would lose its underpopulated quality as former Druj subjects joined Varushka and founded new vales there.
r.Ossium/Echofell: If wagon raiding led a major victory, Echofell would lose its under threat quality, with the Tower of the Scorpion becoming the centre of a garrison keeping the woods clear of orcs and dangerous insects.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Mentioned in passing: explorers from northern Galath Fields might easily stray across the forest border into Thule territory.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: If supporting the settlers led a major victory, Nearweald would lose its under-developed quality as its vales received vital support and supplies.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The spider-haunted Webwood held the worst Druj enclaves, a miasma pillar and Arhallogen's temple, which the Conclave had declared the eternal's property. Wagon raiders might take charge of the region but risked clashing with Arhallogen's followers, and settlement there was excluded under the settlers' action.

Bones in the ocean.d: A contract between Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra and Speaker Morna allowed up to a hundred justicars to settle on the Isle of the Osseini. Visiting Freeborn found that Saltbinder Grekodh's Grendel coven had built a white granite and mithril tower over the regio, destroyed the ghost-binding pillars and killed the justicars left behind. The priests were permitted an enclave on the northern coast. The Senate could commission a Sanctuary of the Justicars for 15 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, on the Isle or elsewhere in the Brass Coast. Shantarim's corsairs proposed a fleet-powered spy network; Ka'bal, Bearer of the Imperial Wayleave, built it during the Winter Solstice.

n.Grendel: A Grendel coven under Saltbinder Grekodh now holds the heart of the Isle, having destroyed the pillars and killed the justicars there. They grudgingly accepted a Freeborn enclave, while a corsair spy network was built to watch them in Feroz.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the justicars are described as a legacy of the Brass Coast's Highborn roots, comparable in skill to a Highborn Steward of the Dead, and Highguard is named as a nation where ghosts are more common.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun orcs are noted as a risk to any sanctuary built on the battlefields of the Iron Plains in Segura.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn priests regained a foothold on the Isle of the Osseini, and the nation was offered a sanctuary to gather its few exorcists under an appointed Justicar. The corsairs of Shantarim got the chance to strike back at the Grendel through a new spy network.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is named as a nation where ghosts and hauntings are far more common than in the Brass Coast.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the ghosts adrift in the Bay were once drawn to and trapped by the Isle's pillars, and with the pillars gone nothing now calls them there.
t.Feroz: Under Grendel rule, Feroz now hosts a small Freeborn priestly enclave on the Isle of the Osseini beside an orc coven's tower. During the Winter Solstice a fleet-supported spy network was built there to watch Lord Rahab's Grendel.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman was put forward as a safer possible site for the Sanctuary of the Justicars, offering isolated but reachable locations.
t.Madruga: Madruga was proposed as a possible site for the sanctuary, and its corsairs, idle since the peace treaty voided the Broken Shore Bounty, were noted as eager to act against the Grendel.
t.Segura: Segura's Iron Plains were proposed as a sanctuary site, being perhaps the most haunted place in the Brass Coast.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Isle of the Osseini lies here, now shared uneasily between Saltbinder Grekodh's coven and a Freeborn enclave on its northern coast, with Grendel escorts requested for visiting ships.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: the Spring 383YE briefing records the Grendel landing pushing down into Fontargenta.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Mentioned in passing: the Spring 383YE briefing records Grendel landings and pillaging along the Oranseri coast between Oran and Joharra.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The peaks of Braydon's Jasse were suggested as an isolated but reachable site for the Sanctuary of the Justicars.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The windswept plains of the Jade Range were suggested as an isolated but accessible site for the sanctuary.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Uninhabited islands in Calvos Sound were suggested as a sanctuary site that would strengthen the justicars' bond with the sea.
r.Segura/Iron Plains: The haunted battlefields of the Iron Plains were proposed as a sanctuary site for studying the dead, though at some risk from Jotun orcs.

Cloud waves break.d: The mist eroded or altered less vital memories but left names, loyalties and ambitions intact. Hearth-magic wards kept it at bay, and citizens were urged to renew friendships, receive anointings, renew oaths and share stories of modern heroes in the Navarr manner. Some embraced the forgetting to begin new lives. Arcane Mark, Cast Off The Chain of Memory, Infant Starts with a Blank Slate and Transmogrification of the Soul's Echo worked differently during the Solstice. Red-masked tulpas traded memories with willing people everywhere except Varushka. Records suggest similar episodes in 346YE and 296YE. The Thule sought the eternal Sadogua's counsel and were told the mist meant nothing and would pass.

n.Highguard: Devorah of Twin Suns, a Highborn magister from Syrene, discovered that washing the hands in pure water while rejecting it within ten minutes dispels the false memory created by Cast Off The Chain of Memory.
n.Navarr: The Navarr practice of Songs and Stories was held up as a model for resisting the fog, Navarr blood mages found blood and water refusing to mix, and stridings reported record numbers walking away from lives in which they felt trapped.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: sutannir are among the storytellers encouraged to gather and share tales of modern heroes at the Solstice.
n.The League: In Temeschwar, troupe magicians performing The Lament of the Shepherd fell silent together and recited strange, sorrowful lines during a ritual for the cicisbeo Guild of the Steel Quill.
n.Thule: The fog plagued Thule lands, and the warlock Urnamost, emissary of Tathenon the Gyre, paid Sadogua four measures of dragonbone only to be told the mist portends nothing and will pass.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: learned magicians 'from Urizen to Wintermark' suggested covens, sects and banners renew their binding oaths at the Solstice.
n.Varushka: Varushkans sleeping in warded homes reported no fog in their dreams, the tulpas did not manifest there at all, and Varushkan blood mages saw blood and water refuse to mix while cabalists distrusted the tulpas for refusing hospitality.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is named among the lands whose magicians urged oath-renewal, and skalds are among the storytellers encouraged to share tales.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the eerie glowing fog that shrouded the Bay in late 379YE and early 380YE is contrasted with this Empire-wide mist.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named, though Lyceum scholars are credited with discovering the empowered Arcane Mark.
t.Hercynia: The Hercynian blood-magic coven Tears Unshed Shall Dry discovered that adding Beggar's Lye to Infant Starts with a Blank Slate strips all knowledge from a willing subject, freeing them to learn anew.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named; it is touched only by the fog that spread to every corner of the Empire.
t.Temeschwar: At the Bloody Great Theatre, performers of The Lament of the Shepherd simultaneously began reciting unsettling lines that no one could afterwards recall beyond a sense of past sorrow.

Construct Arbor of the Twin Roses.d: Proposed by Weirwater and seconded by Reikos, the self-funded motion commissioned a sinecure as described in the Draw strength from vulnerability Wind of Fortune. It created the Voice of the Twin Roses, elected annually by the Dawnish National Assembly and revocable by it. Non-standard costs applied: 8 wains of white granite, 8 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns in labour, with three months to construct. After the Winter Solstice, Claude Deeds provided 4 thrones along with the weirwood and white granite. Once completed, the Dawnish National Assembly will be able to appoint the Voice of the Twin Roses.

n.Dawn: Dawn gains a monument to its exemplar Elayne Silverlark and a new title, the Voice of the Twin Roses, which its National Assembly will elect annually and may revoke once the Arbor is complete.

t.Semmerholm: The Arbor of the Twin Roses is to be built in Semmerholm, with materials supplied by Claude Deeds after the Winter Solstice and three months needed to construct it.

r.Semmerholm/Ferrond: Ferrond is the site of the new sinecure honouring Elayne Silverlark, built from white granite and weirwood.

Construct College of Maykop.d: The motion, proposed by Volodmartz and seconded by Ossium, authorised construction of the College of Maykop in Casinea at a non-standard cost of 20 wains of white granite, 10 wains of mithril and 60 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. It passed. After the Winter Solstice 383YE, Dagon Barossa supplied the 10 wains of mithril, the 20 wains of white granite and 6 thrones 4 crowns, and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos added a further throne. Once completed, the work creates the title of Bursar of the House of Spirits, a Highborn national Bourse position appointed annually through the Tally of the Votes.

n.Highguard: Highguard gains a new national Bourse position, the Bursar of the House of Spirits, once the college is complete, with the holder appointed each year through the Tally of the Votes.

t.Casinea: Casinea is the site of the new College of Maykop campus for the Halls of Maykop, a three-month project built from white granite and mithril.

Construct Healing House of Wittal Grove.d: Proposed by the Senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Mitwold, the motion passed at 328 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Kallavesa. Non-standard costs applied: 56 wains of weirwood and 14 thrones in labour. Vauraus Korppitkotka and Rane Shardbearer each provided 7 thrones and 28 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox 384YE. Once completed, the great work will provide a shared bounty to all herb gardens in Kallavesa. The motion omitted the optional Imperial title, Grimnir of Wittal Grove, which was intended to be held by a grimnir. The constitutional court let the commission proceed and raised an administrative motion allowing the Senate to abrogate the title. That motion failed.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a healing great work in its territory of Kallavesa, and its grimnir, who have committed time and resources to the House, keep the intended title Grimnir of Wittal Grove after the Senate declined to abrogate it.

t.Kallavesa: Proposed by Kallavesa's own Senator, the Healing House will provide a shared bounty to every herb garden in Kallavesa once it is completed.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Wittal Grove is the site of the new Healing House, which was funded through donations of weirwood and thrones after the Spring Equinox 384YE.

Construct Imperial Consulate.d: The motion followed the opportunity described in the All the news from Twin Town Wind of Fortune. It passed at 250 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Tassato. The project carried non-standard costs: 25 wains of weirwood, 15 wains of white granite, 80 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Winter Solstice, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato provided 10 thrones along with the full 25 wains of weirwood and 15 wains of white granite. Once the Consulate is complete, the Imperial Consul will receive regular diplomatic briefings and have access to mercantile support similar to that enjoyed by ambassadors.

n.The League: A major Imperial institution was commissioned in a League city at the initiative of Tassato's senator, and the building materials and some funds were supplied by Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato.

t.Tassato: Tassato was chosen as the site of the new Imperial Consulate, and 250 thrones were disbursed to its senator to build it, with the weirwood and white granite supplied by Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato.

Construct Kauppahall.d: The senator for Hahnmark proposed the motion and Skarsind seconded it. It followed the Apples from a tree Wind of Fortune. Kauppahall cost 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns in labour, took three months to build, and was passed at 84 thrones, which were disbursed to the senator for Hahnmark. Hengest Dun supplied the weirwood and 4 thrones after the Winter Solstice. The motion said Wintermark senators would appoint the title unanimously, but the Constitutional Court ruled this unconstitutional because the role mainly concerns acquiring bourse resources. The Court raised an administrative motion to have the Talon appointed by Tally of the Votes, and it passed. The hall was due to be finished shortly before the Spring Equinox 384YE.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a new trading hall and the title of Talon of Kauppahall, though its senators lost the unanimous right to appoint it once the Court required appointment through the bourse by Tally of the Votes.

t.Hahnmark: Kauppahall was built in Hahnmark at its own senator's proposal, using weirwood and thrones provided by Hengest Dun, and was due for completion shortly before the Spring Equinox 384YE.

Construct Lyceum Schloss.d: Proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by the senator for Karov, the motion authorised the Commonwealth to construct a schloss for its citizens visiting the Lyceum, with the building ceded to the Commonwealth. The construction did not count towards the limit on commissions. Non-standard costs applied: 40 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood and 100 crowns in labour. After the Winter Solstice 383YE, Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen provided 12 thrones 4 crowns along with the granite and weirwood. Once complete, the Lyceum gained a permanent improvement in the speed with which it can codify rituals designed to enchant an army.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's senator for Madruga proposed the motion allowing a foreign power, the Commonwealth, to build and own a schloss within Brass Coast lands near Siroc, strengthening the Lyceum based there.

t.Madruga: A Commonwealth-owned schloss was to be built on the island east of Siroc in Madruga, and on completion it improved the Lyceum's ability to codify army enchantment rituals.

Construct Parador of Dust.d: Proposed by the senator for Kahraman and seconded by Holberg, the Winter 383YE motion commissioned a ministry at the Parador of Dust. Its holder, the Mistress of the Dust Parador, would have the power to purchase mithril and the responsibility to use it for the benefit of the Freeborn people. The commission was self-funded at non-standard cost: 16 wains of white granite, 32 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Winter Solstice, Bakar i Riqueza provided 4 thrones and the 16 wains of white granite. Once complete, the title is to be appointed through the Bourse by Tally of the Votes.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a new ministry whose Mistress may buy mithril for the benefit of the Freeborn people, built on an opportunity offered by their own merchants and paid for by Bakar i Riqueza.

t.Kahraman: Kahraman's senator proposed refurbishing the Parador of Dust within the territory as a mithril ministry, and the motion passed.

r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Parador of Dust in the Jade Range was to be refurbished over three months with 16 wains of white granite, becoming the seat of the Mistress of the Dust Parador.

Construct Runic Hearth of Adamant.d: The Runic Hearth of Adamant is a door to be placed at the bottom of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets. It is meant to stop the trogoni amassing an army there to threaten Hahnmark, Temeschwar, Upwold and Miaren. Its non-standard cost was 10 wains of mithril, 25 ingots of green iron and 25 ingots of orichalcum. The announcement named Torbrytan Dunning, Delver of the Depths, and Brianne Stormborn as the providers. The progress record shows Tobrytan Dunning supplying all of the materials after the Winter Solstice 383YE. The commission did not count towards the limit on commissions. Once completed, the seal still has to be installed in the sinkhole.

n.Navarr: Navarr's territory of Miaren is one of the four lands the seal is meant to shield from a trogoni army rising out of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.
n.The League: The League's territory of Temeschwar is among the lands the ward is intended to protect from trogoni massing below ground.
n.The Marches: The Marches' territory of Upwold is named as one of the lands threatened by the trogoni that the Runic Hearth is built to guard against.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Hahnmark is among the threatened lands. The materials were provided by Torbrytan Dunning, Delver of the Depths, and Brianne Stormborn.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is named as a territory at risk from a trogoni army gathering in Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, which the sealed door is meant to prevent.
t.Miaren: Miaren is one of the four territories the Runic Hearth of Adamant is intended to protect from trogoni emerging from below.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar is listed among the territories the trogoni could threaten if they amass an army, which this ward is designed to stop.
t.Upwold: Upwold is one of the territories the seal at the bottom of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets is meant to safeguard against a trogoni host.

Construct Sweetwater Springs.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Bastion, the motion commissioned a great work following the plans set out in the wind of fortune "The DOOM that came to Sarvos". It passed at 150 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Sarvos, and creates no Imperial position. Construction required 20 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour, and was expected to take three months. After the Winter Solstice Gancio di Catazar provided all of these materials and the labour costs. Once completed, the Sweetwater Springs will give a shared bounty to all herb gardens in Sarvos.

n.The League: A League city gains a commissioned defence against fire, its senator received the 150 thrones disbursed, and Gancio di Catazar supplied the granite, weirwood and labour costs needed to build it.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos is to gain a network of wells and fountains guarding against fire, and once completed the Springs will grant a shared bounty to every herb garden in the territory.

Construct expansion of Georgie's House.d: Proposed by Ossium and seconded by Sarvos, the motion sought to exploit increased demand described in the wind of fortune A health to the company. It required no construction slot but counted towards the limit on commissions, and was to be self-funded by the Withering Gaze at a non-standard cost of 23 crowns. The motion passed. Once completed, the expansion would raise the seasonal income of the Custodian of the Kennels by 100 rings to 388 rings. The motion itself declared that no rat would henceforth be safe.

n.The League: A League sinecure, the Custodian of the Kennels, stands to gain once the expansion is complete, with seasonal income rising to 388 rings as Holberg's kennels sell across the Empire.

t.Holberg: Georgie's House in Holberg was approved for expansion by buying up neighbouring properties, extending the reach of a Holberg business to clients across the Empire.

r.Holberg/Holfried: The Kennels of Holfried were approved to grow into adjacent properties, with construction funded by the Withering Gaze.

Construct spy network in Feroz.d: The commission was made by announcement rather than a vote, after the Senate had previously amended the power of the Imperial Orc Wayleave specifically to allow it to commission a spy network. Non-standard costs applied: 5 wains of weirwood and 10 crowns in labour, three months to construct, and an upkeep of 2 thrones per season. After the Winter Solstice 383YE, Tog provided 2 thrones 4 crowns and the 5 wains of weirwood towards the project.

n.Grendel: The spy network was to be built in Feroz, a territory then held by the Grendel, giving the Empire a source of intelligence in Grendel-controlled lands.

t.Feroz: A special spy network was commissioned in Feroz, taking three months to construct, while the territory was held by the Grendel.

Construct the Tenebrous Path.d: Proposed by Hercynia's senator and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion framed the sinecure as a way to inspire wisdom in Navarr thorns who aspire to command, as the Empire raised its first army dedicated to fighting the vallorn, Isaella's Dance. The project required ten wains of mithril, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. Rhisiart Heartsbane supplied six wains of mithril after the Winter Solstice 383YE, then four more wains and 2 thrones 2 crowns after the Summer Solstice 384YE. Nathair Autumngale added 2 crowns. Once complete, the generals of Navarr may appoint the Wisdom of the Tenebrous Path as a Navarr national title.

n.Navarr: Navarr gains a new national title, the Wisdom of the Tenebrous Path, which its generals appoint and which is intended to guide thorns who seek a general's banner in the fight against the vallorn. Navarr citizens Rhisiart Heartsbane and Nathair Autumngale funded the work.

t.Hercynia: Hercynia's senator proposed the motion, and the territory becomes home to the Tenebrous Path sinecure and its supply of mana crystals.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the motion notes that the anti-vallorn army Isaella's Dance would muster at Miaren the following summer.

r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: The Tenebrous Path sinecure is built in Old Ranging, which became the site of the mana-producing structure tied to the Wisdom of the Tenebrous Path title.

Daughters of the Empire.d: Highborn priests argued that tradition demands every Throne have a memorial in the Necropolis, and that Britta's shrine fell quiet because its purpose was unclear. They proposed a Highborn mandate naming one virtue tied to one of her deeds, plus a Senate motion costing 20 crowns of labour to alter the shrine and turn the Guardian of Britta's Shrine into the Guardian of Britta's Memorial, appointed by the relevant Virtue assembly. Sister Sarah of the Suns of Couros enacted a mandate for Courage, and the Senate amended the title and approved the alterations. Abigail of Ira's Shield proposed an Echoing Obelisk with an Archivist title. Frederick di Sarvos met several people at the summit about Lisabetta's tomb, with no clear outcome yet.

n.Highguard: The Highborn assembly and congregations drove the debate over Britta's memorial and passed the mandate for Courage. Highborn archivists also championed the proposed Echoing Obelisk to keep forgotten soldiers remembered.
n.The League: The League architect Frederick di Sarvos was invited by Ruth of the Cenotaph to design Empress Lisabetta's tomb. He postponed his trip to the Commonwealth and came to Anvil to hear proposals, refusing to meet Cardinal Viviane de Coeurdefer or Ranae de Rondell.
n.Wintermark: Britta remains an undisputed inspiration to the Winterfolk, and only a few grumbled that she was not interred in the Necropolis. Her memorial was rededicated so that her inspiration would reach the wider Empire.

t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Empress Britta's body rests in the marshes of Kallavesa, where it was moved from the Necropolis.
t.Necropolis: Britta's quiet shrine in the Necropolis was rededicated as a memorial to her Courage, with Senate-approved alterations, so it could become a place of pilgrimage again. A new Echoing Obelisk beside the Silent Obelisks was also proposed there.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: a young pilgrim in the story comes from Sarvos, and the architect at the centre of the Lisabetta tomb proposal bears the name Frederick di Sarvos.

Decommission Ossium spy network.d: Cayleb of Felix's Watch, the Imperial Spymaster, made an announcement to deconstruct the spy network then active in the Varushkan territory of Ossium. The page lists standard costs for the work, given as 5 thrones, with decommissioning expected to take three months. No progress or outcome is recorded on the page.

n.Varushka: A spy network operating within the Varushkan territory of Ossium was announced for decommissioning, removing that Imperial intelligence presence from Varushkan lands.

t.Ossium: The spy network active in Ossium was set to be dismantled over three months at a cost of 5 thrones, following the Imperial Spymaster's announcement.

Everything has a price.d: Grendel ships began arriving in Imperial ports on the Bay of Catazar via Oran and Apulus, and the Treasury expected tax revenues to rise. Governor Rahab opened Oran to Imperial fleets, although sanctions in both directions cut their profits. Having lost its Druj trade, Wind Speaker Gwindhon offered mithril for weirwood through a proposed Broken Shore Mithril Market, and urged a costly embassy in Cargo for Fleet Master Esteban. Achan of the Fort Fuil Merchants of Bonds offered to trace named slaves for payment. Maistir Bradach planned to visit Anvil. An Imperial Wayleave commissioned the Mithril Market, but after Feroz was evacuated Rahab's fury withdrew every other unused opportunity.

n.Druj: Under the treaty the Grendel may no longer trade with the Druj, ending a lucrative route that had exchanged Grendel mithril for Druj weirwood. That mithril was now offered to the Empire instead.
n.Grendel: The Salt Lords, Wind Speaker Gwindhon, Achan and the Gainmeachdubh Merchant Adventurers all sought profit from the new peace, through Oran, a mithril market, an embassy, slave searches and a visit to Anvil. They faced the threat of an Imperial embargo, and Governor Rahab later withdrew the unused offers in fury.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay was listed as one of the southern ports where the Broken Shore Mithril Market could be built.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel acknowledged the Empire's punishing wars against the Jotun as a reason funds might be short.
n.The Brass Coast: Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra, as ambassador to the Broken Shore, was offered a grand embassy in Cargo and a role naming captives for Achan to trace. Freeborn enslaved in Feroz began to be returned, while corsairs objected that Oran sold Freeborn goods seized in Feroz's fall.
n.The League: Sarvos was one of the two trade hubs Gwindhon favoured for the mithril market, and Trivento received freed slaves taken during the Grendel occupation of Sarvos in 380YE.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named on the page and is linked only through the wider question of Imperial trade with the Grendel.

t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel vessels began arriving at Imperial ports on the bay, coming via Oran and Apulus, and trade across its waters slowly grew.
t.Feroz: Governor Rahab opened the port at Oran to Imperial fleets, selling Feroz herbs and seized liao, and Freeborn enslaved during the invasion began to be returned. After the evacuation of Feroz, Rahab's fury ended the unused opportunities.
t.Madruga: The first freed Freeborn slaves were escorted over the border into Siroc by Stone Born, and Siroc was named as a possible site for the mithril market.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay was suggested as one possible port for the Broken Shore Mithril Market.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page and is attached only through the wider Grendel trade situation.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos was proposed as a site for the mithril market, and groups of former slaves taken during the 380YE occupation were delivered to Trivento each month under the treaty.
t.Spiral: Grendel ships reached Imperial waters by way of Apulus, unloading slaves there first. An embargo would have serious implications for relations with Salt Lord Kaliact.

r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the herbs sold at Oran were said to be native to Feroz.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The port of Oran was opened to Imperial fleets on Governor Rahab's orders, offering herbs, liao and luxuries subject to stern tariffs. Some corsairs urged captains to shun it, or called for an embargo.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay was listed among the southern ports that could host the Broken Shore Mithril Market.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though Sarvos was one of the hubs suggested for the mithril market and Trivento received returned slaves.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus served as the eastern route for Grendel vessels, which disposed of any slaves there before sailing on into Imperial waters.

Excavate Gildenheim Runeforge.d: Proposed by the Bastion senator and seconded by the Kallavesa senator, the motion followed the Conduit to Destiny wind of fortune. It authorised the careful transport, preservation and removal of the Gildenheim runeforge ruins to Runegrott, Hahnmark. The work required 12 thrones in labour costs and three months. After the Winter Solstice Baal provided 11 thrones and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos provided 1 throne, meeting the cost. Once the excavation is complete, building a runeforge in Runegrott will need 30 fewer wains of white granite and 60 fewer crowns.

n.Wintermark: The Senate formally recognised Wintermark's runesmiths as the rightful heirs of the old runeforge, bringing its remains under their care for a future runeforge in Runegrott.

t.Hahnmark: The salvaged ruins are to be brought to Runegrott in Hahnmark, where they will cut the cost of building a runeforge there by 30 wains of white granite and 60 crowns.

Faded from the winter.d: Dreams sent to briars, traced to the magicians of Urizen's Greenfountain Spire, failed thanks to Synod judgements against briar prejudice and for vigilance. Skirmish opportunities arose against a Spire band at Beaten Branch Wayhouse in Therunin, and against the Varushkan Cabal of the Green Mother, blamed for the Rivers Run Red curse, at Gildenroad in Hercynia. Two further strikes targeted Heirs: the Fellorich Striding at Needlestead, holding a stolen heirloom, and the Greenstride Steading at Tower's Edge Holt, holding captive Winter vates. Scouts at the Liathaven spy network could probe the Heirs' leadership. The Senate ordered magistrates to investigate Yaw'nagrah's cults, causing widespread disruption.

n.Highguard: Highguard's Grey Pilgrims supported the forces fighting the Heirs, tipped off scouts to the Twisting Hive in Summersend, and brought word of the captive Frozen Steps coven at Tower's Edge Holt.
n.Jotun: The Jotun held at least two northern regions of Liathaven, battered by both the war with the Empire and the vallorn; a large scouting force there might learn how they were responding to the Heirs.
n.Navarr: The Heirs were disaffected Navarr, many of them briars, and Navarr lands bore the brunt; vates, stridings and steadings were offered chances to free captive vates and recover the Promise of Home, which could lead to the lost Vate's Shelter.
n.Urizen: The Greenfountain Spire, a Urizeni spire drawing disaffected briars, was identified as the source of the Yaw'nagrah dreams, and its magi and sentinels marched openly with vallornspawn under Agrippina of Green Fountain.
n.Varushka: The Cabal of the Green Mother, Varushkan schlacta and cabalists from Miechernya calling themselves the Twisting Hive under Roman Andrevich, was blamed for laying the illegal Rivers Run Red curse.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Heirs of Terunael are said to have previously tried to stir the vallorn here.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia, freed from Rivers Run Red by the Brackensongs' Rivers of Life, saw opportunities to confront the Cabal of the Green Mother at Gildenroad and the Fellorich Striding at Needlestead.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven was named as the source and refuge of the Heirs, where defeated members fled; stationing scouts at its spy network before the Spring Equinox could reveal their leadership.
t.Morrow: The Greenfountain Spire, hidden in Morrow's Peregro, was revealed as the source of the briar dreams, and a band of its magi and sentinels left Morrow for Therunin.
t.Therunin: Therunin, saved from Rivers Run Red by the Great Forest Orcs, faced a Greenfountain Spire band with vallornspawn and the Greenstride Steading holding captive vates, and both became targets for Imperial strikes.
t.Volodmartz: The Cabal of the Green Mother, which cursed Hercynia in Yaw'nagrah's name, was said to come from northern Volodmartz, with its cabalists from Miechernya.

r.Hercynia/Northpines: Fenella Fellorich's striding, linked to many attacks in the territory, was located at a hideaway in Needlestead, offering a chance to kill her and recover the stolen Promise of Home.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: The Twisting Hive and a herald of Yaw'nagrah were found in Summersend and could be confronted at Gildenroad; the Marshstalker Steading's wayhouse there had been raided by the Fellorich.
r.Morrow/Peregro: The Greenfountain Spire is said to lie hidden in Peregro's mountain pine forests, and its magicians were blamed for the dreams sent to briars across the Empire.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: A Sentinel Gate conjunction near Beaten Branch Wayhouse offered the chance to confront the Greenfountain Spire band and kill its powerful magicians.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: The Greenfountain band vanished into the vallorn miasma of Sweetglades, then emerged openly serving Yaw'nagrah alongside spawn, ettercaps and husks.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: At Tower's Edge Holt the Greenstride Steading held the Frozen Steps coven captive, forcing them to find ways to shield vallornspawn from Winter magic, and the Empire had a chance to free them and kill Clevorn Greenstride.

From the sieve of your hands.d: Despite the Black Plateau's oppressive aura, Grendel forces took all of Spiral. The Salt Lord ruled from Apulian and promised the spires their rights and assets in return for hospitality and first refusal on surplus mana. While cooperation lasted, personal resources avoided the conquered territory penalty and Spiral's scholars helped the Doyen of the Spires codify rituals, though the Grendel would learn what was being worked on. She offered to let Spiral's Urizen support the failing Citadel Guard for six months in return for the secret of the Block's protective mithril ward. She threatened to destroy the Block or seize the spires if refused. Alcuin enacted the cooperation mandate, backed by Veikko Bondforger as Cardinal of Loyalty.

n.Druj: The Druj in Zenith became the Grendel's new neighbours. The Salt Lord sought to contrast her rule with theirs and began fortifying Ossuary against them.
n.Grendel: Grendel armies claimed all of Spiral under Salt Lord Mahiri Kaliact, at a cost from the territory's madness and despair. Urizen cooperation promised her trade, wealth and easier fortification work, and she sought the secret of the Block for her own settlements.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizens left in Spiral faced Grendel rule, and the Assembly chose to urge them to cooperate and trade. Meanwhile the Citadel Guard kept crumbling for lack of territory, with the Salt Lord's offer the only temporary reprieve on the table.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: listed in further reading on the wider Grendel situation in the Bay and opportunities there for the Empire.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: referenced in further reading as a Grendel-held territory in a situation both similar to and very different from Spiral's.
t.Morrow: Many Urizen displaced from Spiral had already made new lives in Morrow, and soldiers leaving the Citadel Guard joined fellow exiles there. Abandoning Spiral would have strengthened the territory further.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt sheltered many exiles from Spiral, and the Salt Lord's emissary appeared on its border to propose her bargain over the Block. An exodus from Spiral would have reinforced it.
t.Spiral: The whole territory came under Grendel control. The remaining Urizen spires were offered a cooperative détente, which the Assembly endorsed, while the fate of the protective Block hung on the Empire's answer to the Salt Lord.
t.Zenith: Druj-held Zenith now bordered Grendel Spiral. Urizen would need to reconquer several regions there, already damaged by the destruction of the Golden Cascade, to save the Citadel Guard.

r.Spiral/Ankra: Ankra had been ceded to the Grendel under the treaty, and their armies moved in to claim it. Its citizens had two seasons' grace to leave.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The Grendel consolidated their hold on Apstrus, and slave caravans hauling white granite were reported heading north through it towards Ossuary.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Salt Lord established her court at Apulian on the southern coast and sent emissaries across Spiral from there, as the Grendel consolidated their hold on the region.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Ateri was one of the regions ceded to the Grendel by the Senate, and orc armies moved in to claim it.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion was ceded to the Grendel, and the Salt Lord's proclamation was delivered to half its spires. It was home to the Block, the mithril ward the Grendel coveted and threatened to destroy.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Grendel forces moved to take Ossuary. The Salt Lord set about fortifying it against the Druj, securing the Legacy and the Twilight Gate.
r.Spiral/Screed: Screed, the source of the oppressive aura of the Black Plateau, was among the regions the Grendel moved to take control of.

Hard times come again no more.d: After the Senate declared Ossium's orcs foreigners and the Synod sought to bring Pride to Ossium, refugees reached Skarsind, claiming abandoned Wintermark farms and clearing new land. A statement by Skywise Fal urged the Imperial Orcs to welcome them, and the spirit of Grud the Unshackled persuaded many to join the nation along the way. Three septs held back. The Ethengraw in Gildermark want their own smithy-armouries. The Illarawm in Southpine want a Synod mandate respecting their ancestor beliefs and an ossuary. The Yerende in Solvihill want a palace of flowers and plants. If two septs join, Skarsind could support a third orc army. Stormcrow Skred later enacted the Illarawm mandate.

n.Druj: The refugees fled centuries of Druj cruelty in Ossium, and each sept had secretly kept its warrior, ancestral or herbal traditions alive in defiance of its former Druj overlords.
n.Imperial Orcs: The nation gained many new members and a more prosperous Skarsind that its people now call home. It also faces three septs whose demands for edifices and a mandate could, if met, bring fighting arts, ancestor lore, apothecary skills and a possible third army.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Grud is glad Arl's teaching lacks the reincarnation beliefs he had heard from Jotun thralls.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named, though orcs from Ossium, a territory it partly held, left for Skarsind.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the three-mile train of soldiers and orc refugees travelled along Varushka's roads on its way to Skarsind.
n.Wintermark: Ossean newcomers claimed farms and forests abandoned by Wintermarkers who had returned to their nation, and ever fewer Wintermarkers remain in Skarsind.

t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw recalled that when Imperial warriors crossed from Karsk into western Ossium, the Druj sent them to face the Empire first.
t.Ossium: A great many of Ossium's orcs left between the Autumn Equinox and Winter Solstice for new lives in Skarsind, taking their tools, seeds and, in the Illarawm's case, the bones of their ancestors.
t.Skarsind: New orc villages sprang up across the territory, making it prosperous and bustling, and three foreign septs settled in enclaves in Gildermark, Southpine and Solvihill. Its people would now fight any attempt to give it up.

r.Ossium/Bittershore: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw were forced to farm northern Bittershore under the Druj.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Mentioned in passing: the Yerende sept once lived in the Drownbark Forest.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Mentioned in passing: the Illarawm sept lived in the Echofell before the Druj rose.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw were made to work as subsistence farmers on the Galath Fields.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Mentioned in passing: the Yerende sept once lived in the Nearweald.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Mentioned in passing: the Illarawm once lived in parts of the Webwood.
r.Skarsind/Gildermark: The warrior Ethengraw sept settled here and would join the Imperial Orcs if an armoury-smithy costing 60 wains of mithril and 120 crowns were built and ceded to them.
r.Skarsind/Solvihill: The herbalist Yerende sept settled here and seek a palace of flowers and plants, costing 60 wains of weirwood and 120 crowns, before they will join the nation and share their realmsroot potion lore.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: The Illarawm sept settled here with their ancestors' bones and want a mandate respecting their beliefs, later enacted by Stormcrow Skred, and an ossuary costing 60 wains of white granite and 120 crowns.

Hoist up the thing.d: In Bregasland, three conjunctions offered relief against the Jotun at Jeer's Hay, Trent Tun and Skop's Landing. In Sermersuaq, a raid at Briar's End could strike a Jotun supply line, and three small forays into the Suaq Font could probe a mystery shown in Kallavesi runecasting. At Ocaso Pines in Segura, Jotun reinforcements bound for the Escuta could be stopped. In Hercynia and Therunin, the Empire could strike the Fellorich and Greenstride Heirs, the Twisting Hive cabal and the Greenfountain Spire. Druj warbands with Tortured Souls threatened Semmerholm and Ossium. A captured Illuminate was held in Zenith, and a phantom orc village appeared near Sun's Rest in Ulnak.

n.Dawn: A Druj scouting warband with Tortured Souls was moving through Averlune Chase in Semmerholm, probing Dawnish defences. A vanishing silent orc village appeared near the Golden Sun's encampment at Sun's Rest.
n.Druj: Druj warbands with Tortured Souls were reaving in Semmerholm and Ossium. Having repulsed the Imperial campaign into Zenith, they held captured Citadel Guard soldiers and an Illuminate at Daenorius Rise.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Grey Pilgrims supplied the intelligence behind the strikes at Tower's Edge Holt and Gildenroad. Highguard priests and exorcists were called on to dispatch the Druj Tortured Souls.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm had suffered losses in last stands in Bregasland, and saving Trent Tun could restore up to one hundred soldiers to its strength. Orcs were also among those called to strike at Ocaso Pines.
n.Jotun: Jotun warbands besieged Jeer's Hay, Trent Tun and Skop's Landing in Bregasland, and their Sermersuaq supply line was exposed at Briar's End. Reinforcements meant to rescue the retreating Escuta in Segura faced ambush at Ocaso Pines.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were offered strikes against the Fellorich Striding, which could recover the Promise of Home and gain word of the lost Vate's Shelter. They could also rescue the Frozen Steps vates from the Greenstride steading and confront the cultists troubling Hercynia and Therunin.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs and Black Thorns were driving the Jotun out of Segura. Freeborn were called to destroy Jotun reinforcements at Ocaso Pines before they reached the Escuta.
n.The League: The League was among the nations called to confront the Druj scouts in Semmerholm, who were probing the roads towards Holberg.
n.The Marches: Marchers in Bregasland stubbornly resisted the Jotun, with the people of Jeer's Hay vowing to fight to their last breath. Rosie Little brought word of the siege there.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Greenfountain Spire was exposed as cultists of Yaw'nagrah sending dreams to briars. After the failed Zenith campaign, Citadel Guard soldiers and an Illuminate were held prisoner by the Druj.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Cabal of the Green Mother, calling itself the Twisting Hive under Roman Andrevich, could be confronted at Gildenroad. Druj raiders threatened the pioneers of Ossium, and Varushkan scouts had reported eerie phantom villages in Oerwealt.
n.Wintermark: Kallavesi fought alongside the Summer Storm in Bregasland while thralls scouted West Marsh. In Sermersuaq, the Mark could raid Briar's End and send small forays into the Suaq Font, where the runes Naeve, Ull and Kyrop had been drawn.

t.Bregasland: Three conjunctions offered the chance to relieve Jeer's Hay, save Trent Tun and its trapped Summer Storm unit, and break the Jotun blockade of Skop's Landing amid the confusing fens.
t.Forest of Ulnak: A silent orc village that vanished after dark appeared near Sun's Rest in Oerwealt. A conjunction allowed it to be explored under the Druj miasma.
t.Hercynia: Conjunctions to Needlestead and Gildenroad offered strikes against the Fellorich Striding and the Twisting Hive cabal, who had inflicted a Yaw'nagrah curse on the territory.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Druj scouts in Semmerholm were thought to be probing the roads to Holberg.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Jotun control of the water at Skop's Landing could enable incursions by Hordalant folk.
t.Kallavesa: Human thralls, apparently using stolen Bregas boats, were exploring West Marsh outside Westerhal. Local militia were alerted to deal with them.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the desolation of Liathaven was named as part of the Jotun threat along the western border.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the beaten Imperial armies retreated from Zenith into Morrow, and the Greenfountain Spire band had set out from Peregro.
t.Ossium: Druj raiders, including Tortured Souls, emerged near Marshstand Rise to prey on newly settled vales and threaten army supply trains. A conjunction offered a chance to stop them.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Druj Tortured Souls were first encountered on the battlefields of Reikos, and its citizens know to fear them.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun in Segura were expected to be driven back over the hills into Reinos within a season or two.
t.Segura: With the Jotun retreating, a conjunction to Ocaso Pines offered a chance to destroy reinforcements before they could resupply the Escuta army.
t.Semmerholm: A Druj scouting warband with Tortured Souls moved through Averlune Chase, possibly a prelude to renewed attack from the Barrens.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun massed near Atalaq, and a raid at Briar's End could disrupt their supply trod. Three small conjunctions reached deep into the harsh Suaq Font behind Jotun lines.
t.Therunin: Conjunctions to Tower's Edge Holt and Beaten Branch Wayhouse offered chances to rescue the Frozen Steps vates from the Greenstride steading and to destroy the Greenfountain Spire's cultists.
t.Zenith: After the Imperial campaign was repulsed with close to fifteen hundred casualties, the Druj held Citadel Guard prisoners. A conjunction to Daenorius Rise offered a chance to free a captured Illuminate under the Druj miasma.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Trent Tun faced being overrun with a trapped Summer Storm unit, and a conjunction offered the chance to save both.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: Jotun warriors besieged Jeer's Hay and blockaded the road to the quays at Skop's Landing, and conjunctions were found to both.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt: Amid barely buried remains, a phantom orc village appeared near the Golden Sun's camp at Sun's Rest.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: Fenella Fellorich was believed to be coordinating Heir attacks from Needlestead, where a strike could kill her and recover the Promise of Home.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: The Fellorich had raided the wayhouse of a Summersend steading and stolen its heirloom. The Twisting Hive and a herald of Yaw'nagrah could be confronted at Gildenroad.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Small groups of human thralls were exploring the wildlands outside Westerhal, and militia were alerted.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Mentioned in passing: the Greenfountain Spire's band left Peregro after the Autumn Equinox.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Druj raiders with Tortured Souls preyed on settled vales near Marshstand Rise, where a conjunction offered a chance to stop them.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Jotun reinforcements camping at Ocaso Pines could be ambushed at sunset, and Yellow Chase was expected to be freed soon.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: A Druj scouting force with Tortured Souls moved through the woods to Averlune Chase.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: The Jotun prepared for war near Atalaq. A raid at Briar's End, by the trod south-west of Atkonaroq, could hamper their supplies.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Mentioned in passing: Jotun provisions and reinforcements were arriving in Sealtoq from Stark.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: The Greenfountain Spire's cultists and spawn had attacked settlements here, and a conjunction near Beaten Branch Wayhouse offered a chance to destroy them.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: The Greenfountain band vanished into the miasma of Sweetglades and emerged openly allied to Yaw'nagrah with a host of vallorn creatures.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: The Greenstride steading held the Frozen Steps vates at Tower's Edge Holt, where the Empire could rescue them and perhaps kill Clevorn Greenstride.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Close to fifteen hundred Imperial casualties fell in Clypion, and a Druj warband held a captured Illuminate at Daenorius Rise.

Impossible landscapes.d: Lord Rain agreed to parley with the Spring Archmage and up to four of the Silver Chalice, hoping to resume work on the ritual From the Mountain to the Sea. Ephisis flatly refused to curb the Sanguine Market or name its clients, though the City arranged a meeting with agents of Prospero and Basileus Flint. Roshanwe would not sponsor the Day Archmage's festival of innovation but asked to meet five seekers from five nations. Sung invited particular magicians and the Seer of the Gateway. Adamant's koboldi scouted building projects across the Empire. Kaela would grant her gift to vallorn fighters only if the General Assembly passed a statement of principle by greater majority. Each parley went ahead without obvious harm.

n.Dawn: Ser Fabienne De Miel of Dawn, the Spring Archmage, secured a parley with Lord Rain on behalf of the Silver Chalice. This followed Ser Elienne De La Chasse's successful Declaration of Neutrality, which ended the old enmity with the eternal.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's emissary noted she already grants her gift to Imperial citizens facing lingering torment at the hands of the Druj.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skywise Gralka, the Archmage of Day, was told Roshanwe would not sponsor his festival of innovation. The eternal asked him instead to arrange a meeting between her favoured and five seekers, each from a different nation.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held territory of Liathaven is one of the places where Kaela said she could readily offer her gift to those fighting the vallorn.
n.Navarr: Kaela offered her gift to those battling the vallorn in Navarr's Hercynia and Therunin. She would act only if the General Assembly passed a statement of principle urging acceptance of her gift by greater majority.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Adamant expressed pleasure that the College of Engineering in Temeschwar had at last been completed.
n.Urizen: Autumn Archmage Edmundo of Damakan's Forge was rebuffed by Ephisis over the Sanguine Market bounties, which threaten Livia of the Spire of Celestial Cascade among others. Night Archmage Elyssiathain received Sung's offer of parley, and Livia was invited to attend both meetings.
n.Wintermark: Sung specifically asked that at least one Wintermark Mystic join the Night Archmage's delegation, which would shape the topics the eternal discussed.

t.Brocéliande: Kaela said she could extend her gift to those facing the vallorn in Brocéliande without difficulty, but only if the General Assembly endorsed it.
t.Hercynia: Since Kaela already holds the Conclave's amity, nothing would stop her blessing vallorn fighters in Hercynia once the General Assembly passed the statement she required.
t.Liathaven: Kaela said she could reach those fighting the vallorn in Liathaven without difficulty, provided Imperial priests gave their explicit approval through the General Assembly.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's koboldi celebrated the completion of the College of Engineering in Temeschwar.
t.Therunin: Kaela offered to let those fighting the vallorn in Therunin call on her gift, reducing their bodies to dust the vallorn could not use, if the General Assembly requested it by greater majority.

Ratify treaty with Thule Winter 383YE.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Madruga, the motion ratified the treaty presented by the Ambassador to Otkodov. It passed. Under its terms the Otkodov Thule would provide three armies for a full year against the Jotun in Sermersuaq, cede back any territory they captured there, return captured Imperial citizens, offer non-citizen Jotun thralldom or death, and spare Imperial settlements. The Empire agreed to let the Thule use protective rituals such as Rivers of Life and not to use powerful rituals of slaughter in Sermersuaq. The Thule noted a missing agreed clause, that Imperial armies would always outnumber theirs in Sermersuaq. Rak said they would still abide by the treaty, but any imbalance would be for the ambassadors to negotiate.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard held Casinea, whose name appears in a garbled form in the treaty's title ('the Casinea Empire').
n.Jotun: The Jotun became the target of a new Imperial–Thule military alliance in Sermersuaq, and any non-citizen Jotun captured by the Thule would face the choice of thralldom or death.
n.Thule: The Otkodov Thule gained Webwood and Miechernya in exchange for committing three armies against the Jotun for a year, and they won the right to send representatives to Anvil to coordinate military matters.
n.Varushka: Varushka lost two regions to the Thule, Miechernya in Miekarova and Webwood in Ossium. The treaty required their people to be peacefully moved to other Imperial regions.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's war against the Jotun in Sermersuaq gained three Thule allied armies. The treaty promised the return of captured Imperial citizens and that Imperial settlements would not be targeted, but the Empire gave up powerful slaughter rituals there.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the name Casinea appears only in the treaty's heading, 'Treaty between Otkodov and the Casinea Empire'.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova lost its region of Miechernya, which was ceded to the Thule under the treaty.
t.Ossium: Ossium lost its region of Webwood, which was ceded to the Thule under the treaty.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov's Thule agreed the treaty with the Empire, committing three armies and gaining two neighbouring Varushkan regions.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq became the theatre of the new alliance. Thule armies would fight the Jotun there and cede any captured territory to the Empire, and the Empire agreed to allow Thule protective rituals but to use no powerful rituals of slaughter there.

r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Miechernya was ceded to the Thule, and its people were to be helped to move to another Imperial region.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Webwood was ceded to the Thule, and its people were to be helped to move to another Imperial region.

Seize the moments.d: With Ossium conquered and the Druj on the back foot in the Forest of Ulnak, the Imperial Orcs could seize the moment. Their Assembly could choose between a war of annihilation under the Summer Storm and a liberation under the Winter Sun. Ambition and Vigilance could add their blessings. The Great Forest Orcs and the Montanians might also be persuaded to help. Dawn could either shun the orc advance or issue an open challenge. At the Winter Solstice, Lochias's Vigilance mandate was upheld but lacked liao, so it was not enacted. Tobias Field's Dawnish challenge was upheld, granting bonuses to armies campaigning in the Barrens for the next year.

n.Dawn: Tobias Field of House Orzel's mandate was upheld. It challenges every nation to prove its claim to the Barrens by taking the most regions, and gives Dawnish armies extra natural resupply in Dawnish territories after campaigning there for at least a year.
n.Druj: The Druj, who hold the Barrens firmly, became the target of a proposed Imperial Orc campaign, with options ranging from their annihilation to inciting their orc slaves to revolt.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's Reikos is noted as bordering the Heart of the Peytaht and as the target of a Druj surprise attack in 367YE.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Udoo's call to claim the Barrens opened two competing strategies for the nation's armies, conquest or liberation, each requiring the Summer Storm and Winter Sun to commit fully. The resolution does not record either mandate passing.
n.Navarr: The displaced Great Forest Orcs live in Navarr lands and have promised to fight alongside the Navarr, and their warchief Vallack was expected at the Winter Solstice as a Navarr guest. The Navarr guide Wyl of the Golden Pines urged the Ambition assembly to back the campaign.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun was stationed in Segura and would need to move to reach the Barrens.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm was stationed in Bregasland and would need to move to reach the Barrens.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: killing Druj in the Barrens is described as meaning fewer to brutalise the Urizen in Zenith.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the conquest of Ossium is cited as weakening the Druj and as showing the cruelty they inflict on enslaved orcs.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm was located in Bregasland at the time.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Heart of the Peytaht forest is described as touching Brocéliande.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were on the back foot here, and slaying Druj in the Barrens would mean fewer to ambush the Dawnish in the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: its recent conquest is cited as weakening the Druj and revealing their cruelty to enslaved orcs.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos borders the Heart of the Peytaht and suffered a Druj surprise attack through that forest in 367YE.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun was located in Segura at the time.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens became the focus of rival plans to conquer or liberate it from the Druj. Under the enacted Dawnish challenge, the nation whose armies take the most regions there is to hold the rightful claim, with bonuses for armies campaigning there for at least a year.
t.Therunin: The displaced Great Forest Orcs and their Montanian allies have taken refuge in Therunin. The page notes it as a southern route into the Barrens if Dawnish territories were closed to the orc armies.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are said to brutalise the Urizen in Zenith.

r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The surviving Great Forest Orcs, who know how to bypass the malignant Heart of the Peytaht, are living in the Lower Tarn Valley and might be persuaded to aid an Imperial Orc incursion.

Signs and sigils.d: The roots of Llofir's lingering forest were consuming the Sign's trenches, which would be destroyed within six months without action. Every mana site in Tamarbode had vanished when the Garden of Llofir was destroyed. Three preservation routes were offered: a Senate motion costing 20 thrones plus 1 throne a season, an army of at least four-fifths strength spending a season clearing the forest, or a Highborn Assembly mandate backed by liao. Graciana also proposed three Winter commissions: beacons yielding Winter vis, a trapped woodland and hostel producing Barren Watchtower potions, or a drowning moat creating a powerful Winter regio and the Conclave title Consort of the Drowning Man. Sela of the Suns of Couros enacted the preservation mandate.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj once used the Sign's Spring regio for their magic, and the dead Druj Ghulai Greenmask was rumoured to have bound himself to it.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Highborn Assembly answered Brother Vashti's earlier call by enacting Sela of the Suns of Couros's mandate for Highborn chapters to preserve the Sign of Tamar, and Highborn Winter magicians helped draw up Graciana's proposals.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr magicians were named, alongside Highborn, as likely visitors if the trapped woodland made the Sign a minor Winter regio.

t.Reikos: Reikos's great Sign of Tamar was being eaten away by the forest Llofir left behind, and a Highborn mandate was enacted to preserve it, while proposals were laid out to turn it into a source of Winter magic.

r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode had lost its Spring regio, Tamar's Toes and every other mana site, but the Sign of Tamar there was found to hold enormous Winter potential and was to be cleared and tended by Highborn chapters under the new mandate.

Smoke and oakum.d: Statements by Brother Hugh and Friar John of the Mourn, urging yeomen to take up arms and neighbours to tend their fields, won sympathy but few backers, since Marchers' identity is bound to their land. Many felt that clearing Alderly to raise a fifth army would be a better course. Sister Elspeth's privateering boast proved impractical, but it prompted the idea of a land raid on Hordalant, Skallahn or the unnamed 'King's Pantry'. Henry Fletcher enacted a mandate to prepare a raid on Skallahn after the Spring Equinox. Maarit Suvidotti and Corey Wayfarer enacted supporting mandates for Wintermark and Navarr. Abbot Matilda separately proposed a history monastery in Ashbrook for a Convener, costing 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns. A no-favouritism proviso would halve that cost.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: cited as one of the foes against whom the Freeborn honed the corsair traditions the Marchers lack.
n.Jotun: Their occupation of Bregasland spurred Marcher plans to raid their homelands and draw their attention, and possibly some of their grand champions, away from the offensive. Skallahn was chosen as the target.
n.Navarr: Soldiers of the Quiet Step, billeted in Upwold, offered their knowledge of routes through Liathaven. Corey Wayfarer's mandate urged the Navarr to aid the Marcher raid with scouts and pathfinders.
n.The Marches: Marchers refused to abandon their farms to fight the Jotun but rallied to the idea of a raid, which Henry Fletcher set against Skallahn. The assembly was also offered a revived Convener of the Assembly to guide its priests.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk fighting in Bregasland pointed out the route from Kallavesa to Skallahn. Maarit Suvidotti's mandate urged Wintermark, especially the folk of Westerhal, to aid the raid across the Gullet.

t.Bregasland: The Jotun presence in the Bregas swamps was the root of the Synod's calls to arms, and the raid aimed to pull Jotun attention away from the territory.
t.Hordalant: It was one of three possible raid targets. The Empire's map would have allowed precise targeting, and Mathilda Fisher claimed to have lived in its marshes, but it was not chosen.
t.Kallavesa: Its West Marsh offered a crossing over the narrow straits to Skallahn, the route the Jotun had once used to invade, now proposed for Marcher and Westerhal raiders.
t.Liathaven: The Quiet Step held that small groups could still slip through Liathaven to Hordalant, and the uprooting of the vallorn from the Westwood opened a path to the King's Pantry.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: past Conveners from Mitwold or Upwold faced accusations of bias from rival Marcher households.
t.Mournwold: Marchers recalled wanting the Jotun gone from the Mournwold, and many argued that clearing Alderly forest to raise a fifth army was the better defence.
t.Skallahn: It was chosen as the target of the Marcher raid after the Spring Equinox. The territory is rich but poorly known, home to the town of Kierheim, and raiders would rely on scouts and Westerhal memories unless a map was secured.
t.Upwold: The Quiet Step was billeted across Upwold, working its farms. Ashbrook was proposed as the site of a monastery for a revived Convener of the Assembly.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the regions the Jotun temporarily held.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the regions the Jotun temporarily held.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: It was the proposed crossing point for raiders heading into Skallahn with the help of Marcher fisherfolk and Westerhal ships.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: The Navarr suggested raiders could pass through Liath's Ring by marsh boat on the way to West Ranging and Hordalant.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: It formed the onward leg of the proposed Navarr-guided route from Liath's Ring into Hordalant.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: With the vallorn uprooted from the Westwood, it became possible to travel from the Marches into the unknown King's Pantry.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Many Marchers argued that the assembly should see the forest of Alderly cleared so a fifth army could be raised.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Mentioned in passing: recalled from Emperor Guntherm's campaigns as low-lying farmland and fisheries, part of the scant knowledge of Skallahn.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Mentioned in passing: remembered from Emperor Guntherm's stories as 'the great plains of the Iron Stand'.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Abbot Matilda proposed building a monastery dedicated to Marcher history between Ashill and the Woldstone, to house a Convener of the Assembly.
r.Upwold/Birchland: Mentioned in passing: named in the myth of the first Marchers emerging from its forests to see Upwold's grasslands.

Some heavenly music.d: After the Grand Library of Canterspire was ceded to Phaleron, Urizeni custodians came forward with grimoires. The architects of Delving wanted a Senate appraisal of new fortification sites. The Hall of the Newborn Sun wanted a Synod statement on auras. The Bleak Tower wanted the Silver Chalice to drop one of its four goals. The sword scholar Helos wanted fifty doses of liao. The sentinels under Lutia of Willstone offered The Guardian Gate freely, asking only for a General Assembly call to retake Zenith. Olic the Wanderer would share the Concordance of Earthbound Stars if Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths were cast by the end of Autumn 384YE. The Book of the Restless Spirit was not added because its statement was never raised. The Conclave then added Gift of Knowledge to Imperial lore.

n.Druj: The Druj are blamed for overrunning the Hall of the Risen Sun and burning the Gardens of Pallas and Morrow, and Urizen's sentinels called for every nation to unite to drive them from Zenith.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel hold Ankra, Cinion and Ateri under the peace treaty, which has sent Urizeni refugees west and put the Court of the White Fountain back on the front line.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn armies helped some inhabitants of the Hall of the Risen Sun flee when the Druj came, and the stargazer Olic planned a sabbatical in Casinea.
n.Urizen: Urizen magicians gained four new grimoires in Urizen Lore, covering fortification, defence, healing, herb lore and curses against priests. The nation's sentinels warned that the Citadel Guard is in serious decline since the loss of Zenith and Spiral.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Olic the Wanderer intended to spend a year or so in Casinea while waiting to see whether Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths is cast.
t.Morrow: Morrow was named among the places the Delving architects wanted surveyed for new fortifications. Displaced priests also planned to found the Hall of the Newborn Sun in the south-eastern mountains near the Three Watchers.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's Delving architects and Willstone sentinels supplied two of the new grimoires. The Stone's Unyielding Defiance ritual will fail permanently if the Court of the White Fountain, now a frontier citadel facing Spiral, is ever destroyed.
t.Spiral: Refugees from Spiral, including Cassirra Greenwell of the lost Fountainhome Spire, brought The Well of Nine Stars west. The architects asked that new fortification sites be sought in Spiral where possible.
t.Zenith: Priests rescued from Druj-held Zenith saved the Book of the Restless Spirit, and Zenith refugees helped found the Bleak Tower. The sentinels sought a General Assembly call for all nations to retake the territory.

r.Morrow/Caeli: The Gardens of Morrow on Caeli's slopes were burned by the Druj. The Wellspring of the High Peak ritual loses its power if the Spring of the Grey Falls in Caeli is ever harmed.
r.Morrow/Ravion: The Bleak Tower spire, built around the Senate-commissioned arboretum in north-west Ravion, offered The Well of Nine Stars, and it was entered into Urizen Lore.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Mentioned in passing: Tomari is not named on the page, which concerns Redoubt's spires and its western frontier with Spiral more generally.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: Lutia of Willstone, descendant of the battle mage Atallanna of Willstone who wrote The Guardian Gate, was chosen to present the book freely to Urizen Lore.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Mentioned in passing: Ankra is one of the regions ceded to the Grendel by the peace treaty, prompting refugees to flee west into Redoubt.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Mentioned in passing: Ateri is one of the regions ceded to the Grendel by the peace treaty, prompting refugees to flee west into Redoubt.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Mentioned in passing: Cinion is one of the regions ceded to the Grendel by the peace treaty, prompting refugees to flee west into Redoubt.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The Hall of the Risen Sun in Occursion was overrun by the Druj. Its priests, rescued in Spring 383YE, saved the Book of the Restless Spirit, which was not added to Urizen Lore because their statement was never raised.

Stone and stone.d: The opportunities had no time limit unless Adamant was declared an enemy, the Master's powers changed or the College of Engineering in Temeschwar was lost. They were: the Tower of the Dragon for the Summer Archmage; a Deepforge in Gildenheim for Imperial Orc magic items; a Deepwyrm Aerie guarding Srodkoja; three mine-enriching statues in Mournwold, Weirwater and Hahnmark; making the Court of the White Fountain unbreakable; and a Red Iron Door against massing trogoni. The Aerie, Deepforge, Black Boar and Three Magpies later expired. Sagua i'Ezmara, the first Master, commissioned the Door, the Court's reinforcement (completed Summer 384YE) and the Owlbeast (completed 385YE). Dima Vasilyevna Novosad announced the Tower in Spring 387YE.

n.Dawn: Weirwater was offered the Alabaster Owlbeast, a lit statue enriching every mine there with a share of 900 rings, which was eventually built and completed before the Autumn Equinox 385YE.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel Wind magicians were recalled as the destroyers of Fort Mezudan, and Adamant feared for the Court of the White Fountain should hostilities with them resume.
n.Imperial Orcs: The koboldi offered to turn the accursed runeforge ruins beneath Gildenheim into a Deepforge making magic items for orc champions, but the opportunity later expired.
n.Navarr: Northern Miaren was among the lands whose mines and mana sites the koboldi warned could face a trogoni assault from the sinkhole within a year or so.
n.The League: The League's Temeschwar housed the College of Engineering on which these opportunities depended, and southern Temeschwar was warned of the trogoni threat massing beneath the sinkhole.
n.The Marches: The Black Boar statue offered Marcher-owned mines in the Mournwold 50 green iron each season but expired unbuilt, while northern Upwold was warned of the trogoni threat.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule orcs were noted as still interested in acquiring the Gildenheim runeforge ruins, a rival to the Deepforge plan.
n.Urizen: Redoubt's Court of the White Fountain was offered adamant reinforcement, and Urizeni magicians would see it completed when the Ashen Flame coven performed Hammers of the Brilliant Shore in Summer 384YE.
n.Varushka: Miekarova's Srodkoja was offered the protection of deepwyrms in an Aerie above Volchitrava, with potions for the Master of Ice and Darkness, but the opportunity later expired.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark was offered the Three Magpies relief to enrich its mines, which later expired, and southern Hahnmark was warned of a growing trogoni threat from the sinkhole.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the koboldi were noted as having supported efforts to strengthen the Castle of Thorns.
t.Hahnmark: The koboldi proposed the Three Magpies relief on Rodthorn, offering every mine 25 orichalcum and 25 tempest jade, and warned that trogoni massing beneath the sinkhole could threaten southern Hahnmark; the statue opportunity later expired.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the koboldi were noted as enthusiastic supporters of efforts to improve the Walls of Holberg.
t.Miaren: The koboldi warned that a trogoni legion from the sinkhole could attack mines and mana sites throughout northern Miaren within a year or so unless the shaft was sealed.
t.Miekarova: A Deepwyrm Aerie was proposed above Volchitrava and Olodny to guard the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, but this opportunity later expired.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named on the page, which concerns Urizen chiefly through the Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt.
t.Mournwold: The Black Boar statue south of Sarcombe would have given Marcher-owned mines 50 green iron each season, but the opportunity expired unbuilt.
t.Redoubt: The Court of the White Fountain was offered adamant reinforcement to make it unbreakable; the work was announced in Spring 384YE and completed in Summer 384YE.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Adamant Gate, rebuilt with koboldi help, was cited as an example of adamant's unbreakable fortifications.
t.Skarsind: The koboldi proposed repurposing the accursed runeforge ruins beneath Gildenheim into a Deepforge for Imperial Orc smiths, but the opportunity later expired.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Onyx Pass linking Redoubt and Spiral and the ruins of Fort Mezudan were described as context for fortifying the Court of the White Fountain.
t.Temeschwar: The completed College of Engineering here underpinned all the opportunities, and southern Temeschwar was warned that massing trogoni might one day attack its mines and mana sites.
t.Upwold: The koboldi warned that a trogoni legion from the sinkhole could pour out against mines and mana sites in northern Upwold within a year or so.
t.Weirwater: The Alabaster Owlbeast was proposed to give every mine a share of 900 rings and guide travellers through the woods; it was completed before the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

r.Hahnmark/Northspires: The Three Magpies relief on Rodthorn would have been visible across the Northspires, but the opportunity later expired.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: The Deepwyrm Aerie would have defended Srodkoja like a 1,000-strength fortification if directly attacked, but the opportunity later expired.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Mentioned in passing: a landskeeper noted the Old Pig in Freemoor lay on a line with the proposed Black Boar passing through the Singing Caves.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Mentioned in passing: the broken-crowned stag statue High Courage in Green March was cited in a landskeeper's observation about alignments with the proposed Black Boar.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Mentioned in passing: Southmoor is not named, though the Black Boar was proposed for the hills south of Sarcombe in the Mournwold before the opportunity expired.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: The Court of the White Fountain in the foothills of Optarion, guarding the Onyx Pass, was made unbreakable with adamant by Summer 384YE.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Mentioned in passing: the ruins of Fort Mezudan on the slopes of Ateri, destroyed by Grendel Wind magic, were recalled as a warning for the Court of the White Fountain.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: The Alabaster Owlbeast was to stand on a hill in Wickmoor northwest of the Weirwater Vales, lit by two great lightstones, and was completed in 385YE.

Tend to the Flame.d: Only Marcher agents of the Silent Bell could get close to the suspicious Whittlefolk. Their list of ringleaders went to Cardinal Ser Ancél Watcher, and they also warned of Hatred dedicates among Marchers at Anvil. Condemning three-quarters of the named leaders would destroy the sect. Any condemnation would end Whittle's green iron shipments to Tassato, and a leader from Little Mournwold would cause that enclave to collapse. The Synod condemned twelve, including Margaret Whittle of Little Mournwold. The wind proposed a Beater's Hall at Sarcombe to protect the pacifist thralls from bandits. It noted that their reincarnation beliefs still block their admission as Marchers. Marchers also debated a "Declaration of Remorse" and thresher reprisals against curses.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a Silent Bell agent used Dawnish wine as a pretext in Whittle, and the sect's anointing stirred hatred of the Dawnish in him.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Udoo's mandate offered a place to thralls willing to fight, but Irontide Lok's statement rejected the thralls' belief in reincarnation. The thralls reacted calmly and respected the nation more for it, though the statement deepened the doctrinal obstacle to their becoming Marchers.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: as the thralls' former masters who were driven from the Mourn, and as a continuing threat of raiders across the Mournwold border.
