n.The League: The League assembly had refused sanctuary to the Whittlefolk. Under the terms set out, any condemnation ended Whittle's green iron shipments to Tassato, and a sect leader proving to be from Little Mournwold would see that enclave shunned and scattered.
n.The Marches: Marcher Silent Bell agents exposed the Whittle sect, and Marchers at Anvil were suspected of harbouring Hatred dedicates. The Marcher assembly still holds the open mandate to invite the thralls into the nation. Its people feared renewed curses, and the thresher Alisoun Bathwater urged a statement encouraging reprisals against anyone who curses Marcher lands.

t.Bregasland: Marcher magicians feared that if the Conclave lifted the Rivers Run Red interdiction, the Bregas marshes could be cursed next. Bregasland threshers were among those pressing for reprisals against cursers, though its landskeepers were sanguine about Mountain Remembers Its Youth.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: its vallornspawn were described as currently agitated and prone to boiling across into Mournwold.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: its landskeepers were more sanguine than Mournwold's about destroying Mountain Remembers Its Youth.
t.Mournwold: The Whittle sect of Hatred was exposed, and twelve Whittlefolk were condemned for blasphemy and heresy. Bandits preyed on the pacifist thralls, prompting proposals for a Beater's Hall at Sarcombe, and the territory still bore the scars of Rivers Run Red.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: none of the Mournwold thralls planned to move to Skarsind despite the Imperial Orc offer.
t.Tassato: Tassato is home to the Little Mournwold enclave and received seasonal green iron from Whittle. That arrangement would end with any condemnation, and the enclave faced collapse if a sect leader was found among its citizens; Margaret Whittle of Little Mournwold was among those condemned.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: its landskeepers were more sanguine than Mournwold's about destroying Mountain Remembers Its Youth.

r.Mournwold/Green March: Green March is one of the regions where the former Jotun thralls farm, and it is now marked as home to many foreign orcs. These farms have become easy prey for bandits and thieves because the thralls will not take up arms.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Southmoor is one of the regions where the Mournwold thralls are content on their farms, and it is now marked as home to many foreign orcs. These pacifist farmers are increasingly targeted by outlaws and thieves.

The Net of the Realms.d: Megaris of Glowspire offered Meraud's friendship, gifts and yearly regalia to a Churnspire Adjutor if a spire taller than Pakaanan's Tower were built in Peregro and ceded to him. Valeria proposed expanding Highwatch Citadel for Zakalwe's heralds, who would supply resources for use only against the Druj. This was commissioned in Summer 384YE, creating the Polemarch of Highwatch. Balbus relayed Prospero's offer of a Market of Iron and Ash in Willstone selling Autumn vis. Sung offered an upkeep-free, hidden spy network at Oblivion's Edge in exchange for the Night Arbour. Sadogua offered to craft magical items for covens. The Tomb King refused aid, and the Whisperer offered famine. Declarations concerning Agramant were withdrawn.

n.Druj: Zakalwe's heralds offered Urizen Pearls of Manush and primessence, to be used solely in the war on the Druj. The page also notes that the Druj invasion of Morrow drove the Glowspire into introspection.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls that Spiral fell to the Grendel in 331YE, leaving the spire of Oblivion's Edge ruined.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: they are not named, but Meraud's spire had to be declared taller than Pakaanan's Tower, which vanished from Pakaanan's Pass.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe's heralds would abandon Highwatch if a Pearl of Manush were used to enchant an army facing the Jotun.
n.Urizen: Urizen's mandate drew offers from several eternals of titles, vis, regalia, a market, a hidden spy network and coven items, alongside a warning from the Tomb King that the nation had lost half its territory. Highwatch Citadel was later expanded for Zakalwe.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Tomb King contrasted Varushka, almost twice the size it was a decade ago, with Urizen's losses.

t.Morrow: A folly overlooking the Churn geyser was proposed for Morrow and would be ceded to Meraud, who would support a Churnspire Adjutor. The local Glowspire is recovering from the Druj invasion.
t.Redoubt: Prospero proposed a Market of Iron and Ash in Redoubt, allowing direct trade in Autumn vis overseen by an Agent of Ash and Iron.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Pakaanan's Tower, which disappeared from Skarsind's Pakaanan's Pass, was the benchmark Meraud's spire had to exceed in height.
t.Spiral: Sung offered a concealed, upkeep-free spy network based at Oblivion's Edge to watch the Black Plateau and all of Spiral, provided it was ceded to her and given the Night Arbour.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Megaris of Glowspire proposed a white granite and mithril spire overlooking the Churn in Peregro for Meraud, with luxurious apartments for the Churnspire Adjutor.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: Balbus of the Spire of Willstone judged that Willstone could host Prospero's Market of Iron and Ash, with a chamber for trade with the Cities of Iron and Ash.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Mentioned in passing: Pakaanan's Tower vanished from Pakaanan's Pass, and nobody can remember its exact height.
r.Spiral/Screed: Oblivion's Edge in Screed would house Sung's heliopticon spy network, and the Night Arbour below it would be consumed to shroud the spire from enemies if the Conclave agreed.

The hammer and the anvil song.d: Faraden and Axou apothecaries planned a market for narcotic concoctions outside the Forge. Wintermark runesmith Leofraed the Deft proposed a season-long exchange of crafts, and the herald Brazen sought an Anvil auction house to sell three wild-card invitations to Basileus Flint's Game of Cunning and Curses. Varushkan warden Vesela Lechovic brought a sword from the Forest of Ulnak, believed to date from the Freedom Heresy, seeking magical confirmation before auction. The displaced house de Coyne offered talismans and Raise the Standard of War for beggar's lye. Six Imperial weirwood seats and other titles were auctioned, while national titles went to the Tally of the Votes. Visitors met with varying success.

n.Dawn: Ser Sevelan de Coyne and seneschal Robin Counter, from a house driven out of Dawnguard and now camping in Ulvenholm, came to Anvil to trade Summer talismans and rituals for beggar's lye, and hoped to visit the Dawnish camp.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as having displaced house de Coyne from Dawnguard, and the sword was taken while fighting in their territory of Ulnak.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn apothecaries appear only in the in-character story, and the Great Forest at Reikos was one of the weirwood seats auctioned.
n.Imperial Orcs: Orc military captains could elect the Four Seasons' Boneweaver and appoint the vacant Bearer of the Imperial Orc Wayleave through the Tally of the Votes.
n.Navarr: Navarr herb garden owners were to choose who controls the Thimble, the nation's own weirwood Bourse seat, for the coming year.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark runesmith Leofraed the Deft proposed an exchange of hand-made crafts between citizens, to be completed at the Spring Equinox, as a show of the Empire's Pride in its artisans.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Varushkan warden Vesela Lechovic came by a sword with a spiritual aura while fighting here with the Golden Axe, and believed it to be a weapon from the Freedom Heresy.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest at Reikos was among the six Imperial weirwood seats offered at the public auction.
t.Semmerholm: The remnants of house de Coyne were sheltering in Semmerholm, camped in pavilions and tents, after losing their lands in Dawnguard.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: house de Coyne is described as having been displaced from Dawnguard in the Barrens by the Druj.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the Weirwater Vales weirwood seat was among the six Imperial seats offered at the public auction.

r.Semmerholm/Ulvenholm: What remained of house de Coyne was camped in Ulvenholm, halfway between Arnet and the Pits of Brychel, from where Ser Sevelan set out for Anvil.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: Dawnguard is named as the former home from which the Druj drove house de Coyne.

The price of wisdom.d: Synod mandates now needed a greater majority, because the Wisdom Assembly had urged the virtuous Empire-wide to question them and Urizen's sword scholars did the same at home. Options included condemning Sulemaine i Taziel, overruling or recanting the Wisdom Assembly, and Urizeni or Freeborn mandates. At the Winter Solstice the spiritual pilgrimage meant simple majorities sufficed. Rafael Barossa di Tassato enacted the General Assembly mandate overruling the Wisdom Assembly. Galene Netherwatch raised a Wisdom mandate urging continued opposition, and Eurybia Melampus de Tassato enacted a Loyalty mandate joining it, leaving the outcome unclear. Clarice Novarion enacted a Courage mandate, and Clytemnestra enacted the Urizen mandate ending debate over Sulemaine.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the foes the sword scholars of any fortified Morrow temples would be eager to fight.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the foes the sword scholars of any fortified Morrow temples would be eager to fight.
n.Urizen: Urizen's embrace of Sulemaine as the Paragon of Blades meant the sword scholars' opposition to Synod mandates would persist there whatever the General Assembly did. Clytemnestra enacted the Urizen Assembly mandate stating that Sulemaine's enemies are not Urizen's and halting further mandates about her for at least a year.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of the doubt that would follow if the General Assembly reversed its earlier rulings, with people asking whether Wintermark might be condemned for drawing inspiration from its forebears.

t.Morrow: The Senate was offered the chance to fund fortified sword scholar temples across Morrow, ceded to the sword scholars, for 60 wains of white granite, 50 wains of mithril and 220 crowns, taking six months to build. The opportunity lasted until the end of the Spring Equinox 384YE.
t.Redoubt: Sword scholar temples could not be built in Redoubt because resistance from the sentinels there was still too strong.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: sword scholar temples could be funded there if the Empire reconquered Spiral, provided the situation in Urizen had not changed.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: sword scholar temples could be funded there if the Empire reconquered Zenith, provided the situation in Urizen had not changed.

r.Morrow/Peregro: The Temple of the Four Winds in Peregro would be the focus of the proposed commission, becoming a strength 3000 fortification garrisoned by sword scholars and inflicting half again as many casualties on attackers. Once ceded, it would lie beyond the Senate's control.

The virtue of sharing.d: Simon of Haros and Ulla Redstaff would back Houses of Healing in Elerael only after a public inquisition, by a Highborn or Urizeni inquisitor, of those behind accepting Druj aid. Imperial Inquisitor Galene Netherwatch inquisitioned Harwyn Eternal and judged him and the Spring archmage totally vindicated, upheld by the General Assembly. Both then offered support, but the Houses were never commissioned and the chance passed. Hazelelponi's Highborn mandate sent congregations to aid Dark Ranging, about 1,400 strength, yet no Imperial army came. New mandates were proposed: Dawnish and Highborn rewards for units fighting there, a Dawnish congregational sacrifice, and Highborn or Navarr commitments to fight only in Brocéliande. Only the Dawnish reward mandate was enacted.

n.Dawn: Ranae de Rondell enacted the mandate urging Dawnish houses to reward any knight who fights to reclaim Dark Ranging, granting Dawnish units extra crowns and herbs for a year. A congregational sacrifice of votes and liao was also proposed but not enacted.
n.Druj: The alliance by which Druj orcs aided the eternal Arhallogen in Brocéliande prompted demands for public inquisition and condemnation of those responsible, though the Conclave did not condemn the alliance.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregations bore a year-long sacrifice under Hazelelponi's mandate, sending pilgrims and supplies worth about 1,400 strength to Dark Ranging only to find no army there. Mandates were proposed to reward guardians who fight there and to commit Highborn soldiers solely to Brocéliande.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly condemned accepting Druj aid, and Harwyn Eternal faced inquisition and was vindicated. Corey Wayfarer proposed a mandate binding Navarr armies to fight the vallorn until Brocéliande is free, while Highborn pilgrims helped Navarr steadings rebuild.
n.Urizen: An Urizeni inquisitor was named acceptable to conduct the inquisition, and the Urizeni Imperial Inquisitor Galene Netherwatch carried it out, returning a judgement of total vindication.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish troubadour jokes that Dark Ranging is no more Navarr land than Ossium was Varushkan.

t.Brocéliande: The Highborn, Dawnish and Navarr assemblies focused on reclaiming Dark Ranging from the vallorn, but the Imperial armies expected there never arrived, leaving congregational aid to support recovery and the fight against the Heirs of Terunael.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: cited in a troubadour's jest that Ossium was once no more Varushkan than Dark Ranging is Navarr.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places two Dawnish adventurers had travelled through before coming to Brocéliande.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Dark Ranging is the target of the proposed reconquest, with Highborn pilgrims already there and an enacted mandate rewarding Dawnish units that support armies fighting in the region for a year.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Houses of Healing were proposed for Elerael, with backing conditional on the inquisition; support was eventually offered, but they were never commissioned and the opportunity passed.

The winds of fashion.d: Fears of the Doom of Sarvos largely came to nothing. A spate of fires was traced to the Carta du Incendio, whose bravos and leaders were caught and tried. Two weeks before the Winter Solstice, however, an accidental blaze destroyed half the Caricomare waterfront, although the docks kept working. The completed School of Couture made the Mirrored Maschieri title available, but the Senator for Sarvos, Nessetta Constanta, had to decide how it would be appointed. Genia Bourné left a letter for whoever took the title. A League Assembly mandate could make Sarvos the City of Masks, and masquerades were proposed. The Lion's Academy announced a bridge-duelling tournament.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the word appears only in the opening fiction, where a Sarvosan boy likes to rise at dawn.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel piracy is cited as one of the hardships Sarvos suffered in recent years.
n.The League: The League Assembly was invited to embrace Sarvos as the City of Masks, and both egregores urged League citizens to plan a masquerade to celebrate triumph over the Hag Queen. Aureliana di Sarvos went on to enact that mandate.

t.Holberg: The Lion's Academy of Holberg, founded by Brann von Holberg in Adelmar's legacy, announced a bridge-duelling tournament at the summit in honour of the School of Couture. Eight League Free Companies were invited to enter.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos suffered arson by the Carta du Incendio and a fire that destroyed half the Caricomare waterfront, but gained the School of Couture. The mandate that followed renewed it as the City of Masks, averting its threatened doom.
t.Tassato: Merchant princes of Tassato, like those of Sarvos, were making plans for rival masquerades to capitalise on the expected flowering of Pride.

r.Sarvos/Bocche: Mentioned in passing: Bocche is not named directly. The page concerns the city of Sarvos as a whole, its Caricomare docks and the new School of Couture.

Thousands or more.d: The survey found Ossium's forests unusually rich, so forest resources there yield 2 extra measures. Its metals are poor, so mining commissions cost double. The five spoils of war were the Palace of Orieb, the Stinking Market, Marshstand Skerry, the Bonehives and the Field of Glory. Each came with a recommended title and possible upgrades. Marshstand Skerry is a dual Spring–Winter regio tied to Agramant that needs animal sacrifice. The civil service also proposed a port at Bittershore, a barracks at Karantzy in Nearweald and an extension of the Iron Roads across Ossium. It warned that the territory's under-developed state greatly raises labour costs, including those for upgrading the Crawling Depths and for Ketsov's opportunities.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish forces are named alongside Varushkans in the slaughter at the Field of Glory, and a Bittershore port would open an option to expand the docks at Lacre.
n.Druj: The Druj's former holdings in Ossium, including Bleakbane's palace, a Bone Serpent ghulai's skerry and the Amber Scorpion insect farms, were catalogued as Imperial spoils of war.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bonewall Tresshak and Bonewall Koshhok helped win over the freed servants at the Bonehives, and most of the freed orcs left to join the Imperial Orcs.
n.Navarr: The Lower Tarn Valley in Navarr's Therunin was named as one of the few places where a new bonehive could be established, with the Keeper's approval.
n.The League: Holberg's Utterlund or Misericorde, where the Sand Fisher orcs now thrive, could host a new bonehive or a future Semmerlak dock.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule may have slain Bleakbane or her apprentices during the events at Orieb in Spring 383YE.
n.Varushka: Varushkan forest owners in Ossium gain extra production, Varushkan settlers drive the new vales, and the Senate placed all five new titles under the unanimous appointment of the Varushkan senators.
n.Wintermark: Wittal Grove in Wintermark's Kallavesa was identified as a possible site for a new bonehive, with the Keeper's approval.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders from Orieb sell goods taken in daring raids across the border into the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Holberg: Holberg's Utterlund or Misericorde could host a new bonehive, and a Bittershore port could lead to a new Semmerlak dock there.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's Wittal Grove was named as a possible site for a duplicate bonehive, built by separate commission with the Keeper's approval.
t.Karov: Karov already has Iron Roads, and a Bittershore port would open an option to expand the docks at Korotny.
t.Karsk: Wagon raiders from Karsk run the Stinking Market, an Iron Road from Karsk could cross Ossium, and the docks at Ivarsgard could be expanded if a Bittershore port were built.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is cited as already having a road network, unlike Ossium.
t.Ossium: Ossium's resources, five captured structures and development options were catalogued, and the Senate set all five new titles to be appointed by the Varushkan senators.
t.Semmerholm: The Bittershore cove once used for Druj raft attacks on Semmerholm is the proposed port site, which would open an option to expand the docks at Lacre.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: freed orcs at the Bonehives were drawn by tales of Skarsind and left to join the Imperial Orcs.
t.The Semmerlak: A proposed port at Bittershore would raise taxation from the territories bordering the Semmerlak and could lead to expanded docks around its shores.
t.Therunin: Therunin's Lower Tarn Valley could host a duplicate bonehive, built by separate commission with the Keeper's approval.
t.Volodmartz: Wagon raiders from southern Volodmartz trade at the Stinking Market, and settlers from Livardz founded the Karantzy vale in Nearweald.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Misericorde, now home to the thriving Sand Fishers, could host a new bonehive and was named as a likely first site for a new Semmerlak dock.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund was named as an alternative site for a new bonehive or a future Semmerlak dock.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Wittal Grove's mix of forest and marsh makes it a possible site for a new bonehive producing three doses of each substance.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Bittershore, vacated by the Sand Fishers, was proposed for a costly new port that would end its under-developed status and create a Merchant-boyar of Bittershore.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The Drownbark Forest holds three of the spoils: the Palace of Orieb, the rowdy Stinking Market and the dual-natured Marshstand Skerry.
r.Ossium/Echofell: The Echofell's south-east holds the Bonehives, an Amber Scorpion insect farm producing unique narcotic and medicinal substances.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: The haunted Field of Glory in Galath Fields yields marrowort for a Grieftender of the Forgotten, and nearby Ketsov's reassessed fortification options now look costly.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Boyar Irina Karantzy's new vale in Nearweald could gain a barracks and armoury, which would remove the region's underpopulated quality and aid Varushkan armies.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Mentioned in passing: Marshstand Skerry is said to have been abandoned since before the Webwood fell.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Lower Tarn Valley's forest and marsh make it a possible site for a new bonehive, with the Keeper's approval.
r.Volodmartz/Livardz: Mentioned in passing: settlers from Livardz founded the Karantzy vale in Nearweald.

Three celebrations and a funeral.d: An apparently accidental fire wrecked the Bastion basilica, the largest Little Mother orphanage outside Sarvos. Bishop Marianne di Sarvos died in it and was interred in Sarvos, leaving the prelacy vacant with reduced liao and votes. Cesare Enzo Di Trivento used an Imperial Wayleave to commission the repairs. The seminary of Zemress at Calvos drew pilgrims from at home and abroad. Rhaego i Zemress enacted a Freeborn mandate opening the way to replace the Broken Wheel festival. The Calvos pilgrimage mandate was never raised, but a translated Sumaah tale of Zemress was published. The General Assembly upheld Killian Mortére's mandate to consecrate the Academy of Arms. The Maze of Zoria remained available for consecration.

n.Dawn: Adelmar the Lion's birthplace at Weaving and the hall at Arnet were both put forward as shrines to the Dawnish-born exemplar. The General Assembly instead backed the Academy of Arms in Urizen.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a few Grendel orc merchants visiting Madruga reportedly paid their respects to Zemress, whom they call the Demon of the Bay.
n.Highguard: Highguard's city of Bastion lost its great white-granite Basilica of the Little Mother and orphanage to fire. Its repair has since been commissioned.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: they are the only nation whose priests have never held the title of Prelate of the Little Mother.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn saw pilgrims and trade flood to the Zemress seminary, and the Sumaah pressed them over the Broken Wheel. A mandate was enacted giving the nation the chance to seek a replacement festival, and a translated Sumaah tale of Zemress was published.
n.The League: The League mourned Bishop Marianne di Sarvos, a former Cardinal of Prosperity, who was buried in Sarvos. Merchant-prince Francesco Falenjame drew wide criticism for his callous remarks about the fire.
n.Urizen: The General Assembly upheld a mandate to consecrate Adelmar's original Academy of Arms in Redoubt as his shrine, though it was not yet known whether the true liao would be supplied.
n.Varushka: The Maze of Zoria, guarded by Illya Nikovitch Volkov, could be consecrated to Wisdom with true liao, but the page records no such consecration happening.

t.Astolat: Adelmar's birthplace shrine in the town of Weaving was one of three proposed sites for consecration. It was not the option the General Assembly upheld.
t.Bastion: Fire gutted the Basilica of the Little Mother and killed its prelate. The scaffolded shell must be repaired or torn down, and repair was commissioned by Imperial Wayleave.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: an anecdote in the opening fiction recalls a magistrate threatening an arrest in Holberg.
t.Madruga: The seminary of Zemress at Calvos became a bustling pilgrimage site. It boosted the local wine trade and revived talk of shipyards.
t.Miekarova: The Maze of Zoria in Miekarova awaits a possible consecration to Wisdom. The Wisdom assembly's call to pilgrimage there met a mixed reception.
t.Redoubt: The General Assembly upheld a mandate to consecrate the first Academy of Arms in Redoubt as Adelmar's shrine, pending true liao.
t.Sarvos: Bishop Marianne di Sarvos was interred at the chapel of the Little Mother in Sarvos, beside the earlier prelates.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Zemress Islanders visiting Calvos return to their new homes in Segura.
t.Semmerholm: The pilgrim hall at Arnet, marking Adelmar's role in liberating Semmerholm, was proposed as a shrine but not chosen.

r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Calvos Sound's seminary and the Kraken's Bane drew pilgrims from the Empire, Sumaah and beyond. Demand for local wine soared, and the seminary published a translated Sumaah tale of Zemress.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: The Maze of Zoria near Griejezdo in Mieriada could be consecrated to Wisdom. The Heirs of Lepidus stand ready to gather and publish pilgrims' stories of Zoria if it is.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: The original Academy of Arms on the slopes of Mount Siluri is to be consecrated as Adelmar's shrine under the upheld mandate, which carries a resonance of building a legacy.
r.Semmerholm/Ulvenholm: The shrine in the shadow of Arnet, associated with decisive action, was one of the competing consecration proposals but was not upheld.

To curb those raging appetites.d: Lord Rahab imposed draconian Grendel law on Feroz: higher taxes, bans on bearing arms and practising magic, class-based punishment, and enslavement in the salt mines, sometimes of whole families. The treaty lets Freeborn in Afarjasse and Morajasse leave with their possessions until Spring 384YE, but those in Fontargenta, Oranseri and parts of the Cazar Straits face enslavement if they try. The assembly could urge resistance, flight or cooperation. The flight mandate was enacted, opening a chance next season for fleets to smuggle trapped citizens out by sea. Several Imperial titles tied to Feroz were lost, and Freeborn with holdings there could relocate them.

n.Grendel: Lord Rahab and his stone born enforcers are imposing Grendel rule on Feroz with an eye to profit, but the enacted flight mandate will drain the population he hoped to tax and weaken him politically and economically.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly chose to urge their people to flee Feroz rather than resist or cooperate, a bitter blow to Freeborn Pride, while the nation lost several titles tied to the territory and can now support only three armies.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the lost Broken Shore Bounty Bourse seat honoured the corsairs who kept the Bay of Catazar safe.
t.Feroz: Now under Grendel rule, Feroz faces harsh laws and enslavement, and its Freeborn were urged to abandon it; Imperial titles tied to its spice gardens, lighthouse, ilium and temple have lapsed or lost their ministries.
t.Madruga: Madruga is a destination for Freeborn fleeing Feroz, where refugees with kin will be welcomed; the civil service expects disruption followed by increased taxation from new businesses, farms and fleets.
t.Segura: Segura is set to receive Freeborn refugees from Feroz, and the civil service expects that once the disruption settles new businesses, farms and fleets will raise its taxation.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is noted as the other territory under Grendel occupation, discussed in a separate Wind.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: The Grendel have moved soldiers into Afarjasse, whose Freeborn may leave for Madruga or Segura with their possessions until Spring 384YE, though businesses and farms must be left behind.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Freeborn in parts of the Cazar Straits are not covered by the treaty's free movement and risk enslavement if they leave, but the open coastline offers a chance for fleets to smuggle them out.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: The Freeborn of Fontargenta are barred by Rahab's soldiers from leaving and must look to a sea rescue by Freeborn fleets to escape.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Grendel soldiers have moved into Morajasse, whose Freeborn may still leave under the treaty, and the Spice Gardens there are now in Grendel hands, ending benefits for their Imperial keeper.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Freeborn in Oranseri are trapped under threat of enslavement, and the Scorrero Nets Bourse seat and the Celesti Lighthouse title will only return if the Empire retakes the region.

Towers behind the moon.d: Starless shrouds persisted over Ossium and Semmerholm, the Penumbral Veil hung over Madruga and Kahraman, and the shrouds over the Barrens, Spiral and Zenith faded. Strange constellations appeared over Astolat. Winter's Ghosts cursed Casinea, cutting its production by a quarter. Twelve magical fortifications were raised across six territories. The Concordium of Pallas aided the Doyen of the Spires. Eternal news followed: Callidus's High Tontine continued, Sorin set his next trial in Bittershore, and Revel arranged to meet challengers. Tharim recognised a new Keeper, Ylenrith withdrew from contact and Lashonar postponed her game. On the Het's orders, Druj released a hundred slaves at Parel, crediting Danica Lidija van Temeschwar as representative of Mazen.

n.Dawn: Strange magical birds appeared in Astolat's night sky, Semmerholm remained starless, and two heralds of Tharim visited the Castle of Thorns; a brace of tortured Dawnish knights were among the slaves freed at Parel.
n.Druj: The shrouds over the Barrens and Zenith faded, and a small Druj force released a hundred human slaves near Parel on the Het's orders before melting back into the forest.
n.Grendel: The shroud that had hung over Grendel-held Spiral faded away this season.
n.Highguard: A Winter's Ghosts curse ravaged Casinea and cut its production by a quarter, and two score Highborn from an ill-starred crusade into the Barrens were among the freed slaves.
n.Navarr: The Voice of the Quiet Forest wove Spring fortifications of thickets, thorns and branches across Hercynia and Therunin, and generals of Navarr are among those Zakalwe's heralds wish to meet about the Tourney.
n.The Brass Coast: The Penumbral Veil hung over Madruga and Kahraman, and Revel intended to hire space from a Brass Coast family at Anvil to meet challengers.
n.The League: Most of the freed slaves at Parel were League citizens taken from the farms of Holberg over a decade ago, and generals of the League are among those Zakalwe's heralds wish to meet.
n.The Marches: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised castles of mist over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire in Bregasland.
n.Urizen: An Autumn enchantment from the Concordium of Pallas aided Urizen magicians codifying the Doyen of the Spires' ritual, despite the loss of Spiral and Zenith hampering their work; a castle of ice was raised in Caeli and a dozen former Zenith citizens were freed.
n.Varushka: Ossium's skies remained starless, strengthening naga secrecy, and Sorin's next Trial of the Pallid Charm was set for the Regio of the Unquiet Hounds in Bittershore.
n.Wintermark: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised five castles of mist across Imperial marshes, and a Winter castle of ice and granite rose in Northspires in Hahnmark.

t.Astolat: Unfamiliar constellations appeared over Astolat, showing a silver firebird with a rose and a horned eagle, before fading; the Castle of Thorns also received two heralds of Tharim.
t.Bregasland: Castles of mist were raised over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire.
t.Casinea: Winter's Ghosts tormented Casinea for three months, and all its farms, forests, businesses, mines, mana sites and herb gardens produced only three quarters of their usual yield.
t.Hahnmark: A great castle of ice and granite was raised in the hills of Northspires.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia gained a Winter castle in Northpines and Spring fortifications of thickets and thorns in the Glen of Shadows, Old Ranging and Summersend.
t.Holberg: Many of the slaves freed at Parel were League citizens taken from Holberg's farms over a decade ago.
t.Kahraman: The Penumbral Veil, a more traditional shroud, hung over Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised castles of mist over West Marsh and Kallavesa Marsh.
t.Madruga: The Penumbral Veil, a more traditional shroud, hung over Madruga.
t.Morrow: A castle of ice and granite was raised in the hills of Caeli.
t.Ossium: Ossium's night skies remained starless, strengthening naga secrecy, and Sorin's next trial was set for Bittershore.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's skies stayed starless, affecting naga there, and a hundred freed slaves were released at Parel in Estmure.
t.Spiral: The shroud over Spiral faded away, and its loss is said to impede the work of Urizen's Doyen of the Spires.
t.The Barrens: The shroud over the Barrens faded away; some freed Highborn slaves had been captured on an ill-starred crusade into the Barrens.
t.Therunin: Eastring's bayous served as moats for walls of woven branches, and a castle of mist rose over East Ashes.
t.Zenith: The shroud over Zenith faded, its loss hampers the Doyen of the Spires, and a dozen Urizen formerly of Zenith were among the freed slaves.

r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of mist over the fens of Ottermire.
r.Hahnmark/Northspires: A great castle of ice and granite, called from the Breath of Winter, was raised in Northspires' hills.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: A castle of ice and granite drawn from the Breath of Winter was raised in Northpines.
r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: The Voice of the Quiet Forest turned the region's thickets and thorns into Spring fortifications.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: Swathes of thickets and thorns in Summersend were woven into Spring fortifications.
r.Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows: Thickets and thorns in the Glen of Shadows were turned into Spring fortifications.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: Mentioned in passing: the region is not discussed; the name appears only in that of Zakalwe's herald, the Opening Gambit.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: A castle of mist was raised over Kallavesa Marsh by the Sussivari Frost Coven.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: A castle of mist was raised over West Marsh by the Sussivari Frost Coven.
r.Morrow/Caeli: A castle of ice and granite from the Breath of Winter was raised in Caeli's hills.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: The next Trial of the Pallid Charm is due at the Regio of the Unquiet Hounds in Bittershore on the summit's second evening.
r.Semmerholm/Estmure: Druj released a hundred slaves at Parel in Estmure; most are recovering at the House of the Proffered Hand.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of mist over the murky waters of East Ashes.
r.Therunin/Eastring: The bayous of Eastring became moats for Spring walls of woven branches.

Whither the seed.d: Corey Wayfarer's Autumn Equinox 383YE mandate, passed 190-0, sought ways to lift the thirty-year curse. Five options surfaced. Niamh Swan's Rest proposed the Brokers Chain, a single commission with offices in Peakedge Stead, Treji and Seren to stockpile ritual potions. Drustan Brocs Guard recalled that the Jarmish prince Raina Telep of Hordoba may hold a Spring ritual text able to break such a curse. Gethin of Stars End Striding devised a magnitude 30 Spring arcane projection costing 90 rings of ilium. Urizen's Citadel Guard could let the ritual be cast from Anvil. Elin Quiet Words negotiated Kaela's aid, at the price of the Navarr renouncing Liathaven forever.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: cited as having taken Zenith from Urizen, one reason the Citadel Guard is in such demand.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: noted as having gained Spiral from Urizen through a peace treaty.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: their bloody war with the Navarr for Liathaven, and their destruction of Elin's home there, explain why Kaela's price targets that territory.
n.Navarr: Navarr families in Brocéliande face withering births from their own curse, and the nation must now choose between costly routes to lift it, including the bitter option of abandoning Liathaven for Kaela's aid.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Citadel Guard could act as a focus, letting the Navarr break the curse from Anvil if it moved to Brocéliande, but the army is badly needed at home and its future is uncertain after territorial losses.

t.Brocéliande: The curse saps the vallorn but steadily reduces births among the Navarr there, and every option raised aims to lift it from the territory before its thirty years run out.
t.Hercynia: Treji in Hercynia would host one of the three offices of the proposed Brokers Chain, a commission that has not yet been built.
t.Liathaven: Kaela's price for her aid is that the Navarr declare their vigil in Liathaven ended, after which her followers would move to claim the remaining Navarr regions there.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Gethin, who devised the ilium-powered Spring arcane projection, lives at Stars End Striding in Miaren.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: noted as having been ceded to the Grendel by the Senate in a peace treaty.
t.Therunin: Peakedge Stead in Therunin would host one of the three offices of the proposed Brokers Chain, and losing it would break the whole network.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: noted as having fallen to the Druj, weakening Urizen and stretching the Citadel Guard.

r.Liathaven/West Ranging: One of the two regions the Navarr still hold in Liathaven; if Kaela's mandate passed, her followers and grim legions would swiftly claim it, and the Navarr would be expected not to resist.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Still under Navarr control, but would be claimed by Kaela's followers if the Navarr Assembly accepted her price and gave up Liathaven.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Peakedge Stead would house an office of the proposed Brokers Chain, so the network would depend on this region staying in Imperial hands.

Written in salt.d: Axos freed its orc slaves under the Liberty Pact, but they have none of the rights of human citizens. They are forced into menial work and watched with suspicion, and diplomacy has only bred Axou resentment. The Imperial Orcs have few fleets, so a General Assembly or Assembly of the Nine mandate was proposed, sending a priest with 50 doses of liao to urge captains to offer passage. Captains doing so would earn reduced profits. Enough fleet strength could bring most or all of Axos's several thousand orcs to the Empire. This risked a diplomatic incident with the Axou. The Commonwealth meanwhile planned to rescue the orcs itself by the Spring Equinox. After the Winter Solstice, Skywise Gralka enacted the mandate.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Axos are watched by the Axou for any sign of sympathy with the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Axos are watched by the Axou for any sign of sympathy with the Grendel.
n.Imperial Orcs: The nation's reavers answered Skywise Gralka's statement but lacked the fleets to rescue the Axou orcs alone, so Gralka sought and later enacted a wider Synod mandate. Rescued orcs, who are city-dwellers with some magical knowledge, could offer an opportunity for the nation.

t.Skarsind: Imperial Orc reavers offered to escort rescued Axou orcs to Skarsind. If at least 10,000 fleet strength were committed, they would become a significant force there, comparable in impact to the Ossean septs.
